plugins.readme_text: Web profile plugin — host half + browser half. > **English**: [README.md](README.md) | **中文**: [README.zh.md](README.zh.md) --- # DSH Hardware Sandbox **A 3D hardware sandbox for DSH: build the assembly, wire it up, and run your project's own code against virtual hardware.** **Install (from GitHub; this package is not published on npm)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:Noob-stupid/dsh-breadboard ``` Then reload the page. The sandbox registers into the **`main`** slot (the 3D view) and the **`sidebar.panellist`** slot (the panels); `skill/SKILL.md` ships with the plugin, so an agent that has it installed already knows how to drive it. **Like it?** Open this plugin's page in the Plugins manager — its own bottom-right corner carries a small, plain-text link to [give it a star on GitHub](https://github.com/Noob-stupid/dsh-breadboard). It is one transparent line, no box, no banner, and it only ever appears on this plugin's page. Three things make that one line work — all three are in this repository: | Requirement | Where | Note | |---|---|---| | repo topic `dsh-plugin` | GitHub repository topics | makes the repo discoverable in community lists | | a `dsh.bundle` manifest | `package.json` → `"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }` | **without it `dsh plugin add` installs nothing** — and the UI symptom is misleading: the plugin list says "no composition bundle declared", while what actually broke is the assembly, so every `/api/*` returns 404 and the panel simply never appears | | an exported `apply(ctx)` | `src/index.ts` (host) / `src/client/index.ts` (browser) | host half registers routes, tools and the simulation engine; browser half registers the two slots above | ## What it is / what it solves Normally the parts of a hardware project you can only *try on the real board* are the wiring itself, the sensor semantics at register level, and the failure handling. This plugin moves those into a virtual scene that actually runs: - **3D assembly** — drop parts from the built-in model library (ESP32, Raspberry Pi 4B, BME280, HC-SR501 PIR, LED module, MPL3115A2, breadboard), wire them port by port, and get a live SSOT (single source of truth) assembly state with topology and electrical checks. - **Project-level hardware-in-the-loop** — a **real Python process** runs **your project's code**. A Python shim intercepts its `smbus`/I2C access and answers from virtual devices, so the project under test reads register-level values (e.g. it performs the real BME280 compensation math on data coming from the virtual chip). - **Networked-device emulation** (a second, separate class of virtual hardware) — a device that actively POSTs to **your** external HTTP backend on a real cadence: register → pull config → periodic report. Verified end-to-end against a real seat-selection system (device → HTTP → backend state machine → database). - **Failure injection** — unplug a wire, return NACK, force a reading, take a device offline, and watch whether the project's error handling actually catches it. - **Project-level convenience** — scan a real project folder to learn which hardware it needs, and switch the entire hardware setup in one click. Requires DSH with the **`web`** profile and `webServer`, `tools` and `subprocess` services. The host half declares them as **hard `inject` dependencies on purpose**: if any of them is missing the plugin does not activate at all, rather than activating with tools silently unregistered, a blank panel, or a simulation engine that cannot spawn. ### See it without a real project `examples/zhizuo-virtual-esp32/` is a standalone script version of the virtual ESP32 seat sensor. `hw_list_projects` lists the built-in demo project (**zhizuo-seat-node**) together with whether it is currently wired end to end; `hw_import_project` puts its parts, wires and network binding in place in one call. ## UI tour The interface is currently **Chinese only** — the labels below are the literal ones on screen. | Panel | What it does | |---|---| | **③ Project (one-click hardware swap)** | the main workflow. Per project body: file count (`N files (M skipped while sampling)` when sampling skipped files), **Scan requirements**, **Delete**; plus **+ Import project body (pick folder)** and **+ Import model bundle (pick folder)** | | **① Add component** | click a model key to drop it into the scene (collapsed by default) | | **② Re-skin models** | search for a model / import a file, and re-skin one of the model keys above; a model key with no geometry renders as a placeholder box (collapsed by default) | | **Statistics** | render statistics (draw calls / triangles / FPS) — pure read, off by default | | **Center 3D view** | placed components with world transforms, **blue cables** between ports, spatial warning boxes drawn on the components that have `warn`/`error` warnings, gizmo/right-click menu (pin, delete), port tooltips | | **Panel overlay input box** | send a message to the current session without leaving the panel; if the host exposes no `agents` service the box is hidden (`capabilities.chat` is absent) | Two of those deserve emphasis: - **Scan requirements is a UI button only.** It is not exposed as an agent tool — the agent side has no equivalent. What the agent *can* do is everything after that: place parts, wire them, build a project blueprint, run simulations. - **Deleting a project only deletes the project definition** (that one JSON). It does **not** touch the scene, so removing a project never wipes the hardware you have on screen. ## Quick start: three steps 1. **Import the project body** — *+ Import project body (pick folder)*, point it at a **complete project folder** (frontend + backend + hardware code). It is imported **without** models; the host reads it to work out which hardware it needs. 2. **Scan what hardware it needs** — the **Scan requirements** button in the ③ panel (UI only, see above). The report lists each candidate model key with the **evidence** — which files it was seen in — so you can judge it yourself; when the scan had to sample, it says so instead of implying it read everything. 3. **Import a model bundle** — *+ Import model bundle (pick folder)*, a folder laid out as `/model.glb`. Whatever you skip keeps rendering as a placeholder box. Or skip steps 1–3 entirely: describe the system to the agent and let it call **`hw_save_project`** to write a blueprint, then **`hw_import_project`** to place every part, wire and network binding in one go. ## Agent tools: 16 `hw_*` tools This is the actual registered list (nothing added, nothing omitted). The **when to use** column is the point of the table: these tools are not interchangeable. ### Projects | Tool | What it does | When to use it | |---|---|---| | `hw_list_projects` | list built-in hardware projects: parts, wires, network config, and whether each is currently wired end to end | **before** hand-placing anything — a blueprint is one call, hand-assembly is four steps and a missed step fails silently | | `hw_import_project` | import a project: **clears the current assembly first**, then places parts, wires and network bindings | switching the whole hardware set; note it *replaces*, it does not add | | `hw_save_project` | create or overwrite a project blueprint (stored under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-hardware-sandbox/projects/`) | the user described a system in words — write it down as a blueprint, then import it | ### Assembly | Tool | What it does | When to use it | |---|---|---| | `hw_get_assembly` | read the SSOT summary: revision, components, connections, warnings (with their `message`, not just the code), power summary, virtual devices | **before every edit** — you need the real port ids; port ids are pin identities (`E4`), not silkscreen names (`GPIO23`) | | `hw_edit_assembly` | one tool over the contract's `ClientAction` union: place / move / rotate / connect / disconnect / remove / pin | any change to the scene. It takes an action object, so read the samples

plugins.description: 自动开发调度器2.0（dsh-orchestrator2）：DSH agent preset 插件——交互设计 → goal 驱动开发流水线 → 验收修复循环。发布镜像：插件源码 + 最新安装包（当前 v2.9.0）。
plugins.readme_text:
# 自动开发调度器（dsh-orchestrator 系列）

> DSH agent preset 插件：单会话双态——先以调度员身份与你交互完成产品设计（并行研究员调研 → 方案 → 决策清点 → 定稿），一句确认后切换为调度引擎，goal 驱动自动推进开发流水线（审核员计划审核 → 开发员执行自测 → 审核员 AC 证据核验+代码审查 → 调度员构建），推进到「待人工测试」硬停止等你实测；验收阶段走修复循环（T0~T3 证据链）。
>
> **当前版本：v2.10.1**（2026-10-13 发布）　|　**相对上版 v2.10.0 的差异**：codegraph 闭环强制同步——**每次任务完结必须更新代码图谱**成硬规则：任何任务包（含修复包）置「已完成」前，调度员在项目根机械执行 `codegraph sync`，无条件、不分内外层、改了什么就更新什么；未同步不得关闭，验收结论.md 增「codegraph 同步」记录行，关卡3 收尾兜底再同步一次（用户指令 2026-10-13）；规范升 v2.1.6（§六 新增第 7 条闭环门禁 + §六 第 4/6 条与 §2.4 挂引用，经生成器 CG-A~F 六个 op 落地、--check 逐字节校验）；persona 四处同源（A1 连跑前置 sync／新增闭环段／P2-1 修复包前置／收尾门禁 ⓪ 步）＋验收结论模板同步；原子升版（五处版本载体 + pkg-consistency 常量族同候选 commit 切换）。套件 561→561/0（断言数不变）；机器层零改动（dispatch/phase-gate/budget 零改动，不新增状态/环节/角色）。
> **宿主要求**：建议 DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 起（0.1.7 声明式预设机制：包内 `presets/agent-preset.patch.yml` 自动生成预设声明层，无需手工处理）；v2.10.1 实测于 DSH web 版与桌面版（Electron，desktop profile）　|　规范：项目目录及协同开发规范 **v2.1**（六区结构，本文档 v2.1.6）

## 版本与能力速览（v2.10.1）

- **codegraph 闭环强制同步（v2.10.1 新增）**：任何任务包（含修复包）置「已完成」前，调度员机械执行 `codegraph sync`（不分内外层、改了什么更新什么）；未同步不得关闭，验收结论留同步记录行；收尾兜底再同步；codegraph 不可用按降级口径如实标注，不伪造——图谱始终是最新单一事实源
- **模板目录归集（v2.10.0）**：脚手架四区「按任务复制用」模板 21 件收进各区 `_模板/` 子文件夹，区根不再平铺混杂；三级复制源回退（项目内 `_模板/` → 旧平铺位 → 预设包 spec/templates）老项目无损；规范 v2.1.5
- **三阶段工作流**：交互态设计（grill-me 决策清点开场问档）→ goal 驱动单包开发（一次授权多包连跑，五态流水线）→ 验收修复循环（含审核员修复审查）
- **两类任务场景**：新产品全流程 / 修改已有系统（场景1：现状研究中+目标代码区约束）；另有**技术调研储备**（场景2，独立终态不进开发）
- **首次使用引导与开工门禁（v2.9.0 新增）**：新会话首次对话先探查后告知（插件级 3 项＋项目级 6 项，只列缺失/未验证项，零副作用）；按需授权逐项补齐；`enter_auto_mode` 开发准备门禁 fail-closed（`00-项目管理/开发准备.md` 记录不齐即拒并列缺项）；远程仓库/测试服务器允许「不适用」须写理由，codegraph 不自动降级
- **对话形态纪律（v2.8.0 新增）**：全部人读消息 answer-first + 结尾唯一下一步 + 首尾双问自检 + 分组 ≤5（证据优先于简洁）；提问纪律（一次一决策点/选项 ≤4 推荐置顶/优先卡片提问）；过程消息一行制；不采用项成文（状态.md 唯一真源不散文重述／不删限定词／证据·债务清单不设条数上限／输出更短非目标）
- **子代理模型路由与会话覆盖（v2.7.0 新增）**：每角色默认+降级双槽路由（持久配置现读、原子写、不落在预设同步树）；429/额度类错误自动切降级（G1 硬闸门：插件独占先于宿主重试，不消耗默认模型重试预算；降级失败即停不循环；非适用错误不误降级）；会话临时改模（缺省仅当次主会话、epoch 隔离、在跑 child 快照不受影响、压缩不丢）与显式永久改默认/降级（原子保存、新派工即生效）；「仅下一次」一次性语义明确拒绝不落状态
- **挂载防回归（v2.7.1）**：delegation 组本地模块行必须导出 `apply` 的装配断言（config-check T3h，含缺 apply 夹具检红演算）；注册与更新前体检**双 profile 覆盖**（web 走 CLI、desktop 走 Electron 管理）
- **SpecKit 证据裁决口径（v2.6.1 起）**：AC 证据核验表「证据等级/逐项状态」列；修复包未决澄清闸门、根因初判、正当扩围第三态、上游指针；场景2 裁决三态、反证强制与 `ASSUMPTION` 标记
- **运行安全三层机制（v2.4.x）**：派工生成**三问裁定**；开发员**五条刹车纪律 + 心跳**；**看门狗**（B/C 后台派工、调度员轮内 tick 值班，L0 观察→L1 steer→L2 中断→L3 停机）；恢复轮孤儿接管；审核员计划审核第 5 项判断题
- **调度可靠性机器层**：预算台账 = 环节级 WAL/结算账本（schema v2 身份行 + runId/attempt/派工前阶段/结算后阶段/candidateCommit/evidencePath 六列）、runId 精确结算、派工返回六态（DONE/DONE_WITH_CONCERNS/NEEDS_CONTEXT/BLOCKED/FAILED/INTERRUPTED）、dispatch_status 四方一致检查+续跑建议、旧台账 v1→v2 迁移、故障注入五项回归套件
- **质量闸门**：任务包改动点「消费/产出」接口契约 + 计划审核跨改动点冲突扫描；验收「无证或不可证伪即驳回」；修复包 T0 根因→T1 RED→T2 GREEN→T3 回归证据链；代码审查 loadBearing 承重标注；P1-8 审核纪律（不机械重跑/选择性复验/证据缺失驳回）
- **预算纪律**：按包分档三硬上限（小包 4/6/24、大包 8/8/48，派工即计次），token 纯统计、无费用概念
- **与 1.0（orchestrator）并存不替代**：两插件各自独立，按会话独占加载

本仓库为**发布镜像**（只含最新版本）。安装包：`05-交付/安装包/dsh-orchestrator2-v2.10.1/`（或同名 zip 解压到本地目录后按目录安装）。

**web 版（`dsh web`，profile=web，CLI 一条命令）：**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/路径/dsh-orchestrator2-v2.10.1
```

**桌面版（Electron，profile=desktop，由应用专属管理，CLI 写入会被拒 `managed exclusively by the Electron application`）：**

1. 打开桌面版**插件管理**界面（设置 → 插件），添加/更新插件，方式选「本地目录（link）」，指向 `…/dsh-orchestrator2-v2.10.1` 包目录；
2. 若界面不可用或需脚本化，可用**手工三件套**（操作前备份原文件）：① 改 `profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 link 依赖行指向新包目录；② 同步 `pnpm-lock.yaml` 对应两行；③ 把 `node_modules/dsh-orchestrator2` junction 重指到新包目录。

**两端通用**：装完**完全退出并重启**（桌面版注意先退出托盘进程，避免旧实例占端口）；新建会话在预设选择器选「自动开发调度器2.0」。重启前建议体检：`node "$env:APPDATA\npm\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh\lib\bin.js" web --dump-config`——① 组合树含 `preset-orchestrator2`；② 零死引用；③ 注册指向新包。详见包根 `测试入口说明.md` 与包内 `presets/orchestrator2/docs/使用手册.md`。

> 注：0.1.7 起预设走声明式机制（包内 `presets/agent-preset.patch.yml` 在宿主启动时自动把预设声明进组合树）；旧版「裸目录拷贝到 `~/.dsh/.agent-presets`」方式已随 0.1.7 移除，勿再用。

plugins.description: DSH (DeepSeek Harness) browser plugin: give your agent hands inside the Chrome you already use — native messaging + CDP, no TCP port, no Connect button, 9 native browser_* tools.
plugins.readme_text:
English · 简体中文 · Development notes

--- **Give your DSH agent hands inside the Chrome you are already using** — your logins, your tabs, your session. Install once, no Connect button, ever. ![the in-page cursor driving a real page](assets/cursor-demo.gif) Every click flies a cursor to the target and labels what it is doing. It renders *inside the page*, so it lands in screenshots too — you and the model look at the same picture. ## ✨ Why another browser bridge? Every existing option makes you click something, every time: | Option | What goes wrong | |---|---| | `chrome-devtools-mcp --autoConnect` | Chrome asks *"Allow remote debugging?"* on **every** connection | | Browser MCP (store extension) | You must click the extension icon → **Connect** on **every** tab | | WebSocket-based bridges | Open a TCP port and trust anything that can reach it | | **dsh-chrome-bridge** | Nothing to click. Nothing listening on a port. | Three things make the difference: - 🔌 **Native messaging, not a port.** The extension talks to a local Node host over Chrome's native messaging pipe; the CLI reaches the host through a `0600` Unix socket guarded by a token. No TCP port to scan, no origin to spoof. - 🎯 **`chrome.debugger`, not injected scripts.** Clicks and keystrokes are dispatched as real CDP `Input.*` events, so they carry a user gesture — popups open, focus works, and sites that reject synthetic events behave normally. Screenshots, network, console and raw CDP come for free. - 👀 **A cursor the human can see.** A translucent light-blue arrow with a "🌐 DSH" name tag glides along a gentle arc to the target; the tag says what it is doing (click / type / drag / scroll) and each click leaves a soft ripple. It shares one style with the desktop cursor of [dsh-mac-computer-use](https://github.com/OrderG-X/dsh-mac-computer-use) (solid there, with a monitor icon), so you can tell at a glance whether the work is in the browser or on the desktop. It sits above modals and fullscreen, and picks up where it was after a navigation. Because it is rendered inside the page, **it appears in screenshots**. ## 🏗 Architecture ``` DSH's agent (provided by the harness — this repo ships none) ├── browser_* tools (DSH plugin) ─┐ └── cb CLI (shell) ─┤ ▼ Unix socket /tmp/dsh-bridge.sock (0600 + token) ▼ Node native host ←─ native messaging (stdio) ─→ Chrome extension (MV3) │ chrome.debugger ▼ real CDP ``` **This repo ships no agent** — the agent above is DSH's own; we only give it hands. The extension ID is fixed by the public key embedded in `plugin/vendor/extension/manifest.json`, so it is **identical on every machine** and the native-host registration never needs editing. ## 🚀 Install **The host ships inside the plugin package.** Adding the plugin copies the native host and the MV3 extension into place and registers native messaging for you — no `git clone`, no `install.sh`, no `python3`. Requirements: **macOS**, **Google Chrome 116+**, **Node.js 18+**. **1.** Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → paste this → Install → Enable → **restart DSH**: ``` https://github.com/OrderG-X/dsh-chrome-bridge/releases/latest/download/dsh-chrome-bridge.tgz ``` **2.** The plugin installs itself on first load (`~/.dsh/chrome-bridge`, `~/dsh-bridge-extension`, plus `com.dsh.bridge.json` in Chrome's `NativeMessagingHosts`). Loading the extension into Chrome is the one step nothing can do for you — Chrome 137+ removed `--load-extension`, and the Web Store does not accept the `debugger` permission. So the plugin walks you to that click instead: - the first time a `browser_*` tool finds nothing to talk to, it **opens `chrome://extensions` in a background tab** and **puts `~/dsh-bridge-extension` on your clipboard** (once per session; the error text repeats the steps); - in the file picker press **⌘⇧G**, then **⌘V**, then Enter — no folder hunting. Do it once, ever: 1. open `chrome://extensions` 2. enable **Developer mode** (top right) 3. **Load unpacked** → **⌘⇧G** → **⌘V** → Enter (the folder is already on your clipboard) From a source checkout, `./bridge setup` does exactly this in one command: installs the host, opens the page, copies the path, and waits until the extension connects — printing ✅ when it does. **3.** Verify (the `cb` CLI is installed along the way): ```bash cb status # host pid … | extension connected: ✅ cb tabs ``` Until step 2 is done the `browser_*` tools fail **loudly with exactly these steps** — never silently. ### 🧩 The eleven native tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `browser_tabs` | list / find / open / close / activate tabs | | `browser_read` | **numbered list of clickable / fillable elements** (`snapshot`), visible text, HTML, attributes, page info | | `browser_click` | click by element number (`ref`), selector, text, or coordinates | | `browser_input` | type, press keys, select, upload, hover, scroll | | `browser_nav` | go to a URL, **back / forward / reload**, and wait for load | | `browser_screenshot` | screenshot **returned as an image** (viewport / full / element) | | `browser_eval` | run JS in the page | | `browser_wait` | wait for an element, **a piece of text, or a URL** — or for it to go away (`gone`) | | `browser_dialog` | release alert / confirm / prompt | | `browser_drag` | drag by element number, selector, **visible text** or coordinates — HTML5 drag-and-drop and mouse-driven widgets (sliders, sortable lists) | | `browser_devtools` | **console output + uncaught JS errors, network requests (status, timing), a request's response body** | > A freshly installed bundle is not hot-loaded; DSH must be restarted once. > `dsh plugin add` from the CLI refuses the app-managed profile — use the sidebar there. > Plugin updates are not automatic in DSH yet: to upgrade, uninstall and install again. ### 👀 What you see while it works - **Click the toolbar icon** for a live panel: whether Chrome ↔ local host ↔ DSH are connected, **which DSH sessions are driving which tabs** (jump to a tab, or release it with one click), the last actions with their errors, a **pause switch** that makes the browser off-limits until you turn it back on, and *copy diagnostics* for bug reports. The icon badge shows how many tabs are under control (`!` = host down, `⏸` = paused). - **In DSH, Plugins → Chrome Bridge** has a settings card too: connection status, whether the extension is the local or the Web Store build, which tabs are under control (release them all with one click), plus pause and on-page-cursor switches. When it isn't connected it tells you the missing step and can open the install page for you. **Resuming control only works from the Chrome extension panel** — the model can reach the DSH side as well, so that click has to be yours. - Every tab the agent touches **joins a blue tab group

plugins.description: TrustedRouter privacy and routing settings per model for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-trustedrouter

Per-model [TrustedRouter](https://trustedrouter.com) privacy and routing settings for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

For each model, choose a privacy floor, which providers may serve it, what to optimize for, how it's billed and whether providers must be US-based. You do this from **Settings → Models** in the dsh web UI. The plugin adds your choices to every request as TrustedRouter's [`provider` object](https://trustedrouter.com/docs/provider-routing).

![The Privacy & routing section inside a TrustedRouter card on Settings → Models](docs/models-section.png)

## Why a plugin

TrustedRouter reads routing and privacy policy only from the request body, for example `{"provider": {"min_privacy": "confidential"}}`. No header or API-key setting does the same job. dsh's model providers can add headers but not body fields, so without this plugin there's no way to ask for a privacy floor.

## Requirements

- **dsh web**, tested on 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-alpha.1 (see [Tested with](#tested-with)). The desktop app isn't supported.
- **pnpm on your PATH.** dsh installs plugins with it, and fails with "pnpm was not found" otherwise. If you don't have it, run `corepack enable pnpm` or `npm install -g pnpm`.
- **A TrustedRouter provider in dsh.** Settings → Models → **Add model provider** → **Custom model API**:
  - base URL `https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1`;
  - API protocol **OpenAI Chat Completions**;
  - your TrustedRouter API key;
  - the models you want, e.g. `z-ai/glm-5.3`.

## Install

**From the dsh web UI:**

1. Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**.
2. Enter `https://github.com/AmmarByFar/dsh-trustedrouter#v0.1.0` and choose **Install**.
3. Choose **Enable now**. No reload or restart is needed.

**From the command line**, for the `web` profile that `dsh web` uses:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:AmmarByFar/dsh-trustedrouter#v0.1.0
```

Then restart `dsh web` if it was running.

The plugin has no build step, so pnpm doesn't ask you to allow one. Its only peer dependency, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, comes from dsh itself, so the peer warning pnpm prints is expected.

**Installing changes nothing yet.** Requests go out unchanged until you set a policy.

**Upgrading.** dsh doesn't update installed plugins yet. Uninstall the plugin (Plugins → TrustedRouter privacy → **Uninstall**), then install the new tag. Your settings live in your profile, not in the plugin, so they're kept.

## Use

### Per model: Settings → Models

Open **Settings → Models**, find your TrustedRouter card and open **Privacy & routing**.

Each of the provider's models is listed with the policy it gets. Its tag says where that policy comes from:
- **Custom** for the model's own settings;
- **Defaults** when it only has the defaults;
- **Uses \<model\>** for a variant such as `z-ai/glm-5.3:nitro`, which follows its base model unless you give it settings of its own.

**Edit** opens a model's settings:

![Editing z-ai/glm-5.3: a Confidential floor, limited to two providers](docs/model-editor.png)

| Setting | Sends | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy floor | `min_privacy`: `no_store`, `zdr` or `confidential` | Each level lists the providers that meet it for this model. TrustedRouter refuses the request rather than use a provider below the floor. |
| Prefer | `sort`: `price`, `latency` or `throughput` | |
| Only these providers | `only` | Empty allows every provider. |
| Never these providers | `ignore` | |
| Billing | `usage`: `credits` or `byok` | TrustedRouter credits, or your own provider key (BYOK). |
| US-headquartered providers only | `jurisdiction: "us"` | |

As you change settings, the editor counts the providers that still qualify. It warns you if none do, because TrustedRouter would then refuse every request for that model.

**Apply** saves to your profile, and the next request uses it. No restart is needed.

A few things to know:
- The section appears only on saved providers whose base URL is under a configured gateway. By default that's `https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1`.
- You can only change settings from a browser on the same machine as dsh. That's a dsh rule for all settings.
- To list providers per model, your browser fetches TrustedRouter's public model list (`<base URL>/models`, no API key sent) the first time you open the section. If that fails, every privacy level is offered.

### Defaults and advanced settings: the Plugins page

Sidebar → **Plugins** → **TrustedRouter privacy** (under Installed), then the **TrustedRouter privacy** row under Components.

![The TrustedRouter privacy page under Plugins](docs/plugins-page.png)

- **Gateways:** the base URLs the policy applies to, one per line. Add the EU gateway, `https://api-europe-west4.quillrouter.com/v1`, if you use it.
- **Defaults for every model:** the same settings as a model has. A model's own settings override them field by field.
- **Advanced defaults:**
  - preferred provider order (`order`);
  - whether to fall back to other providers (`allow_fallbacks`);
  - maximum prompt and completion prices in USD per million tokens (`max_price`).
- **Per-model overrides (JSON):** every model's settings, including any `provider` field the Models page doesn't show.
- **Raw body rules (JSON):** fields deep-merged into every POST under a base URL, for anything that isn't `provider`.
- **Log changes to the terminal:** see [Check that it works](#check-that-it-works).

### Config file

Both pages write the `trustedrouter` row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. For `dsh web` that's `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, or under `$DSH_HOME` if you set it. You can also edit it by hand:

```yaml
- id: trustedrouter
  config:
    gateways: [https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1]   # the default
    defaults: { min_privacy: zdr }                 # for every model on those gateways
    models:                                        # keyed by model id
      z-ai/glm-5.3: { min_privacy: confidential, only: [tinfoil, privatemode] }
    rules: []                                      # optional [{ baseURL, body }], deep-merged after the policy
    log: false
```

How a request's `provider` is built:
- A model's settings are its entry in `models`, merged over `defaults`. A `:suffix` id such as `z-ai/glm-5.3:nitro` uses its base model's entry unless it has its own.
- The result is merged over any `provider` the request already has, so your policy wins. Lists replace rather than combine.
- Values are type-checked, so a misspelled privacy level or a malformed URL is rejected. Fields the plugin doesn't know are passed through; TrustedRouter rejects unknown options with a 400, so a typo fails loudly rather than being ignored.

## Check that it works

1. Turn on **Log changes to the terminal** (or set `log: true`).
2. Send a chat with a TrustedRouter model. The terminal running `dsh web` prints a line like this:
   ```
   [trustedrouter] added provider to POST https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1/chat/completions for z-ai/glm-5.3: {"min_privacy":"confidential"}
   ```
3. Optionally, prove the floor is enforced. Set **Confidential** on a model no confidential provider serves, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`. The chat should fail with TrustedRouter's 400: `No route candidates match the requested provider filters`.

Repeat step 2 after every dsh upgrade (see [Limitations](#how-it-works-and-limitations)). The log never includes request bodies, only the URL, the model id and the fields added.

## How it works and limitations

- **It wraps the dsh server's `fetch`.** POSTs under a gateway get `provider` merged into their JSON body. GETs, such as model discovery, and requests to other URLs pass through untouched. A request whose model has no policy is sent byte for byte.
- **It fails closed.** If a POST to a gateway needs a policy but its body can't be read, the plugin refuses it rather than send it without the policy. The refusal is always printed to the terminal.
- **It relies on dsh internals.** It works because dsh's model clients use the global `fetch`. If a dsh release changes that, requests would go out without your policy, and nothing would error. Check the lo

plugins.description: Run the local Codex CLI as a peer agent from DeepSeek Harness: split work between the two agents, hand tasks over, review each other's changes, and keep every run on disk.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-codex-peer

[![CI](https://github.com/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer?sort=semver&label=release)](https://github.com/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer?label=license)](https://github.com/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer/blob/main/LICENSE)

Peer collaboration between a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) agent and the local OpenAI **Codex CLI**.

Codex and DSH each keep their own session, tools, skills, sandbox, and model. They are not integrated.
They exchange work through ordinary tool calls and files in the shared working tree, much as two
people on one repository would. One does a pass and the other reviews it. Or one plans and the
other executes.

```
You: "have Codex implement the retry logic, then review what it wrote"
DSH: codex_plan(goal: "add retry logic")          →  the split is recorded as a shared work list
     codex_ask(mode: "implement", prompt: "...")   →  Codex edits the tree, reports back
     codex_review(target: "working-tree")          →  Codex is asked to attack its own diff
     (or the DSH agent writes its own review of the same diff)
```

> **Not affiliated with OpenAI or DeepSeek.** This plugin ships no code from either project: it
> drives the Codex CLI you installed yourself and uses the plugin API DeepSeek Harness publishes.
> "Codex" is a trademark of OpenAI and DeepSeek Harness is a DeepSeek project. You need your own
> Codex CLI installed and signed in; how you use it is your responsibility.

## What it adds

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `codex_ask` | Runs one Codex turn in the session's working directory and returns Codex's final message. `mode: ask \| plan \| implement` decides whether Codex answers, plans, or edits; `continueFromLast`/`resumeThreadId` continue an earlier Codex thread. |
| `codex_review` | Runs one **read-only** Codex turn whose answer must be a structured review (verdict + severity-ranked findings with file and line), produced with `codex exec --output-schema`. |
| `codex_status` | Reports where the Codex executable was found, its version on request, the effective settings, the shared work list (`tasks.summary` plus the open tasks), and the recent runs and resumable threads. |
| `codex_plan` | Agrees and records the split of a goal between this agent (`dsh`) and the Codex peer, as a shared work list both sides read. `goal` is required; `tasks` carries the split when it is already decided. Approving this call approves the plan. |
| `codex_task` | Works that list: `action: list \| show \| claim \| update \| record-evidence \| set-budget \| run`. `action: run` is a normal peer run attached to a task — refused when the task is out of Codex budget, charged against the task, continuing the task's Codex thread, and its outcome recorded as evidence. |

Where the runs and the work list are written is [Where everything is written](#where-everything-is-written).

## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh` peer, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.1`) and Node `>= 20`.
- The Codex CLI, installed and logged in.
- No runtime dependencies, and host-only: the Harness injects its own packages, this plugin declares
  none, and nothing is registered in a client bundle.

### Finding the Codex CLI

The desktop Codex app does not put itself on `PATH`, so discovery walks these candidates in order
and uses the first that exists:

1. `codexPath` from this plugin's configuration;
2. `CODEX_CLI_PATH` in the Codex `config.toml` (the desktop app writes it there);
3. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\*\codex.exe` (newest version directory first);
4. `%APPDATA%\npm\codex.cmd`;
5. `codex` / `codex.exe` / `codex.cmd` / `codex.bat` on `PATH`.

`codex_status` prints the winner, its source, and the candidates it rejected. If a call fails with
`codex CLI not found`, that output says exactly which paths were considered.

## Install

The plugin is **not on npm**, so `dsh plugin add dsh-codex-peer` resolves only once the market lists
it. An entry for the curated
[`awesome-dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry has been
submitted; until it lands, install from GitHub or from a release tarball. Either way the plugin
contributes a `dsh.bundle`, DSH records it in `dsh.profile.bundles`, and a restart (or profile
reload) is required before the tools appear — bundles compose at startup.

```bash
# from the plugin market, once it is listed (or the market's own install button)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-codex-peer

# from GitHub, pinned to a release tag (works today)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer#v0.3.2

# or from GitHub, tracking the default branch
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer

# or from a release tarball you downloaded — works offline, but keep the file where it is:
# the profile records that path, so moving or deleting it breaks the next install
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-codex-peer-0.3.2.tgz

# or from a local clone, when you are working on the plugin itself
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /absolute/path/to/dsh-codex-peer
```

Release tarballs live at <https://github.com/wuanthony397-hash/dsh-codex-peer/releases>.

## Quick start

### Install, restart, verify

1. Install it (any way above) and **restart DSH**. The five tools appear only after a restart,
   because bundles compose at startup.
2. Check the setup by asking your agent *"check the codex peer status"*: it calls `codex_status` and
   prints where the Codex executable was found, the effective settings, and the work list.

Then say what you want in plain language and describe how you want to collaborate.
The agent picks the recipe; you never need to name a mode.

### The six modes

Every mode goes through one tool call. `codex_plan` takes a required `goal`; `tasks` carries a split
that is already decided (each entry takes a required `title` plus `owner`, `acceptance`, `scope`,
`tags`, and `why`), and `budget`, `replace`, `mirror`, and `cwd` shape the rest. `mode` is the recipe
over that same work list.

#### `assigned` — you name who does what

Use it when you already know the split and want it written down. For example: "Split this between you two: Codex does the retry logic, you do the tests."

The agent calls `codex_plan` with `mode: "assigned"`, the `goal`, and one `tasks`
entry per piece, each with `owner` (`dsh` or `codex`), `acceptance`, and optionally `scope`,
`tags`, and `why`. Nothing has to be negotiated, so `propose: "none"` is allowed and skips the
critique.

You get the recorded work list with task ids, owners, and acceptance lines, printed as a
one-line summary per task. `codex_task action: list` prints the same list at any time.

#### `self-organizing` — the two agents decide, by strength

Use it when the split is not obvious, and you want both agents to weigh in before anyone
starts. For example: "Work out between yourselves how to do X."

It calls `codex_plan` with `mode: "self-organizing"`. With the default
`propose: "dsh"`, this agent drafts the split, sends the draft to Codex for a critique under a JSON
schema, folds the critique's risks into the notes, and then records it. `propose: "codex"` lets
Codex draft first; `propose: "none"` skips the critique and records the draft as-is.
You get the recorded work list, plus Codex's critique summary and its risk lines
whenever a critique ran.

#### `pipeline` — staged work

Use it when the work has a natural order and you want each stage to be reviewable on its own. For example: "Do it as a pipeline: plan, implement, review, fix."

The agent calls `codex_plan` with `mode: "pipeline"`, which creates four staged
tasks: `Plan:` (codex), `Implement:` (codex), `Review:` (codex), and `Fix and verify:` (dsh), each
with an owner and an acceptance line.

You get the four tasks in order, each runnable on its own with
`codex_task action: run`, so every s

plugins.description: Evidence-first agent memory and durable mission runtime — UNKNOWN states, immutable belief history, governed learning, and missions that survive kill -9. Zero-dependency TypeScript kernel.
plugins.readme_text:
# credence **MOST AGENTS REMEMBER TEXT. THIS ONE REMEMBERS EVIDENCE.** [![CI](https://github.com/MajidAsghariTabrizi/credence/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MajidAsghariTabrizi/credence/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-black.svg)](LICENSE) [![Node >= 22.6](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.6-black.svg)](package.json) [![zero dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-black.svg)](package.json) `credence` is an **evidence-first agent memory and durable mission runtime**. Not a vector store, not a RAG pipeline, not an orchestrator — the layer underneath all of them: an append-only knowledge ledger where every belief carries its evidence, every correction preserves its history, every learning passes an authority gate, and every mission survives its process. - **You need it if** your agent runs for hours or days, and "remembering" currently means stuffing text into a context window. - **It's different because** knowledge here has *epistemics*: graded support, evidence links, supersession chains, and an explicit UNKNOWN state. An agent powered by credence can answer *"I don't know — and here's the closest thing I do know, and why it doesn't qualify."* ## KILL THE AGENT. THE MISSION CONTINUES.

*(A timed replay of a real `npm run demo:kill` run — those are actual captured output lines and PIDs, not a mockup. Run it yourself below.)* ## Run it in 30 seconds Requires Node ≥ 22.6. No install step, no API key, no model — the whole demo is deterministic and local. ```bash git clone https://github.com/MajidAsghariTabrizi/credence cd credence npm run demo:kill ``` That kill-and-resume is one of four signature moments. Or run them one at a time: | Moment | Command | What you see | |---|---|---| | **I DON'T KNOW** | `npm run demo:unknown` | A question with hearsay but no evidence → `UNKNOWN`, with the reason. No guessing. | | **I CHANGED MY MIND** | `npm run demo:contradiction` | New calibration contradicts old belief → old claim superseded, **never erased**, full chain inspectable. | | **I LEARNED — BUT NOT BY MYSELF** | `npm run demo:governed` | Worker agent proposes knowledge → `DENIED`. Owner commits. The worker then *reuses* what it was denied the right to teach itself. | Or run everything: `npm run demo`. Every headline claim in this README has a test, a command, or a fixture behind it — see [PROOF, NOT PROMISES](#proof-not-promises). ## The five ideas this repo owns ### 1. Memory with epistemics A claim is not a string in a vector. It is a record: ```text claim c_e21f0106 text "star tracker drifts 0.02°/sol after firmware 2.1 recalibration" support measured (measured > inferred > reported) basis "post-firmware-2.1 calibration run GC-CAL-0051" evidence e_cal0051 — 21-sol drift series, slope 0.019, r²=0.99 state active (active | superseded | disputed) supersededBy [] (grows — never rewrites) ``` ### 2. UNKNOWN is a feature `ask` returns `unknown` — with the reason and the nearest rejected candidate — whenever coverage is below threshold or evidence is absent. [Retrieval rule → `src/kernel/ask.ts`](src/kernel/ask.ts) · [Demo → `npm run demo:unknown`](demo/unknown.ts) ### 3. History is immutable Corrections **supersede**. The old claim stays readable forever, linked to its replacement, with the contradiction event between them. [Fold → `src/kernel/store.ts`](src/kernel/store.ts) · [Demo → `npm run demo:contradiction`](demo/contradiction.ts) ### 4. Missions outlive processes Mission state is an append-only log on disk (`keel`). Kill the process; a fresh one folds the log and continues. Mission state is *operational* state — it is never automatically trusted knowledge. [`src/kernel/keel.ts`](src/kernel/keel.ts) · [Demo → `npm run demo:kill`](demo/kill.ts) ### 5. Learning has authority Agents may discover and propose. Only `owner`/`lead` commit durable knowledge. A denied commit is logged, not lost — the proposal waits for review. [`src/kernel/learn.ts`](src/kernel/learn.ts) · [Demo → `npm run demo:governed`](demo/governed.ts) ## PROOF, NOT PROMISES | Claim | Run this | Read this | |---|---|---| | "It says I DON'T KNOW" | `npm run demo:unknown` | [`test/kernel.test.ts` · unknown](test/kernel.test.ts) | | "It changes its mind without deleting its past" | `npm run demo:contradiction` | [`store.ts` · supersession fold](src/kernel/store.ts) | | "Workers cannot commit" | `npm run demo:governed` | [`learn.ts` · authority gate](src/kernel/learn.ts) | | "Missions survive process death" | `npm run demo:kill` | [`keel.ts` · durable resume](src/kernel/keel.ts) | | "Retrieval quality is measured" | `npm run bench` | [`bench/` · fixtures + runner](bench/run.ts) | | "Zero dependencies" | `cat package.json` | — | Benchmarks are synthetic, seeded (deterministic), and honest — [latest results](bench/results.json) on this exact kernel: unknown-detection **1.00**, hallucination-on-unanswerable **0**, paraphrase recall **0.65** (token-coverage retrieval, no embeddings), ask latency p95 **~1.3 ms** at 200 claims. Weak numbers stay published. ## Architecture ```text Agents worker · lead · watcher · operator (propose, never commit) Harness lifecycle · tools · keel missions (durable operational state) Brain ask · explain · investigate · learn · pulse Packs ground-control/ … each an events.jsonl (append-only, one fold away) ``` One process, one directory, zero dependencies. The event log *is* the database — no migrations, no server. [Deep dive → `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ### Deep rabbit holes
What happens when the Brain doesn't know? `ask` scores every active claim by *query coverage* (fraction of your question's content tokens present in the claim) weighted by support grade. Below 0.45 — or any best match with zero evidence — you get `state: unknown` with `why` and the `nearest` rejected candidate. You can then `investigate`: collectors gather findings, split into **durable candidates** (commit via `learn`) and **ephemeral observations** (never commit — a measured value is wrong tomorrow).
What happens when new evidence contradicts old evidence? A `supersede` delta writes two events: `contradiction-raised` (both ids + the note) and `claim-superseded` (old → new). The fold marks the old claim `superseded` and appends the successor id. `explain ` walks the whole chain. Nothing is deleted; the log only grows.
What exactly is allowed to learn? Caller identity is a role: `owner`, `lead:*`, `agent:*`, `watcher`. `propose()` records the delta as a pending proposal; `agent`/`watcher` commits are refused with a `learning-denied` event — the denial itself is part of history. `owner`/`lead` approve with `commitProposal`. Private claims (`sensitivity: private`) are filtered out of agent reads at the store layer.
What survives a dead process? Everything th

## 这是什么 / 不是什么

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ✅ 是 | DSH 当 **ACP 客户端**，驱动外部 CLI（omp / opencode / command-code）当根 agent |
| ✅ 是 | 把 DSH 的 **MCP 服务器随 `session/new` 下发给引擎**（引擎因此能用 DSH 里配好的知识库等） |
| ❌ 不是 | DSH 当 **ACP 服务端**。DSH 内置的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp` 是**反方向**（把 DSH 变成别人的 agent），本插件不复用它 |
| ❌ 不是 | provider 路线（外部 CLI 只当"大脑"，loop 仍属 DSH） |
| ❌ 不是 | 子代理路线（官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-acp`） |

## 配置

`cordis.patch.yml` 的 `config`：

> ⚠️ **改配置前必读**：非 `insert` 的 patch 行按 `id` 定位后是**整体替换**
> 该 Entry 的 `config`（**不是深合并**）。所以 profile 里写一份只含两三个键的覆盖，
> 等于把**其余键清成代码默认值** —— 而且不会报错。
> 本机就因此让 A16 的 `promptTimeoutMs: 0` 从未生效过（见 `docs/ISSUES.md` ISSUE-16）。
> 改完跑 `npm run verify:profile` 核对**实际生效的配置**。

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultEngine` | `''`（**本仓库自带的 patch 里设为 `omp`**） | 没有显式 preset 的会话走哪个引擎；留空 = 走官方 DSH agent loop |
| `stateDir` | `<DSH_HOME>/multi-acp`（patch 里用 `!!js` 展开 `DSH_HOME`/`USERPROFILE`） | 引擎定义、会话映射、`trace.log` |
| `engines` | `[]` | 引擎定义（最高优先级，便于试验） |
| `verboseStartup` | `true` | 启动时打印宿主符号自检结果 |
| `presetTools` | `true` | `acp-*` preset 挂哪些原生工具组：`true` / `false` / `['skills','shell','fs',…]` |
| `unsandboxedFs` | `false` | `true` = 用 entry-local `dsh-fs-local` 遮蔽宿主沙箱 fs（写工作区外不再被拒） |
| `mcp` | `{enabled:true, include:[], exclude:[]}` | MCP 随会话下发策略（见下） |
| `promptTimeoutMs` | `300000` | 一次 `session/prompt` 的超时；**`<=0` = 不超时**（长任务推荐） |
| `trace` | `true` | 诊断追踪 `<stateDir>/trace.log`。`false`/`'off'` = **关闭**；`'<path>'` = 改道。**落盘前一律中央脱敏**（见下） |

**诊断追踪与脱敏**（`lib/trace.js`，v0.2.1 / ISSUE-13）：trace 是排查"factory 有没有装上、preset 注册了没、
引擎走了哪条分支"的主要证据来源，但它落在 `DSH_HOME` 下、又是最容易被贴进 issue 的文件，
所以它是本插件**唯一**的落盘收口点，写之前一律脱敏：

- **按键名**：`token` / `secret` / `password` / `apiKey` / `authorization` / `bearer` / `credential` / `cookie`
  → 整值 `<redacted>`（`sessionId` **故意不在其列** —— 它是诊断主键）；
- **按值的形状**：`sk-…` / `mcp_…` / `gh?…` / `AKIA…` / PEM 私钥 / JWT / `Bearer …` /
  自由文本里的 `token=…`、`--password …`、`密码 <值>` / **邮箱 → `<email>`**；
- **上限**：单字符串 300 字符截断、6 层深、40 字段宽（防整篇 prompt 落盘）；
- **工具调用标题不记正文**（只记 `titleLen`）—— 正文里的凭据实测存在，需要正文时看**会话日志**。

**引擎来源优先级**（`lib/engines.js`）：内置 `BUILTIN` → `<stateDir>/engines.json` → 插件 `config.engines`。
按 `id` 整体覆盖（不做深合并，避免半覆盖导致意外）。引擎行还可单独设 `mcp`（`'inherit'`/`'none'`/自定义数组）
与 `promptTimeoutMs`（优先于插件级）。

### MCP 随会话下发

默认把 `<DSH_HOME>/storages/mcp_connector.json` 里 `enabled !== false` 的连接映射成 ACP `McpServer`
（stdio → `{name, command, args, env[]}`；http/sse → `{type, name, url, headers[]}`，bearer → `Authorization` 头），
随 `session/new` **与** `session/load` 下发。收窄方式：

```yaml
mcp:
  enabled: true
  include: []              # 只下发这些（按 name / serverName / serverKey 匹配）
  exclude: ['dingtalk']    # 排除这些
```

⚠️ 治理边界：ACP 没有审批/授权字段，注入给引擎的 MCP 是**全量可用**的；DSH 的 `tools.governance`
不随之生效。键名以 [ISSUES/ACP-INTEGRATION](./docs/ACP-INTEGRATION.md) §4.1 记录为准。

### 新增一个引擎

```jsonc
// <DSH_HOME>/multi-acp/engines.json
{
  "engines": [
    {
      "id": "mytool",
      "label": { "zh": "我的工具", "en": "My Tool" },
      "command": "mytool",
      "args": ["acp"],
      "cwdPolicy": "session",     // session | fixed
      "mcp": "inherit",           // inherit | none | [自定义服务器]
      "promptTimeoutMs": 0,       // 可选：该引擎不超时
      "enabled": true,
      "sortOrder": 40
    }
  ]
}
```

要求：该 CLI 必须能说 **ACP over stdio**。先用探针验证，再验证 MCP 接受性：

```powershell
cd probe; node probe-acp.mjs "mytool" acp                       # 基础往返
node ..\tmp\probe-mcp-engine.mjs mytool

plugins.description: Keyless-default web search for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): one provider on the ctx.web seam running an ordered fallback chain over Tavily (keyless), Parallel MCP, SearXNG, Brave, TinyFish and Exa. API keys are managed from the web client's Plugins page.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-websearch-stack

[![CI](https://github.com/orfeomorello/dsh-websearch-stack/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/orfeomorello/dsh-websearch-stack/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Multi-provider web search for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh). The plugin registers one search provider on the `ctx.web` seam; that provider runs an ordered fallback chain over the backends you enable.

> **Status**: v0.1.0, MVP. Six backends implemented and unit-tested. Verified live: **Tavily keyless** and **Parallel MCP**. The others need an API key or a local instance and are not yet verified — see [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

## Features

- **Six search backends**: Tavily (keyless-capable), Parallel MCP (no credentials), SearXNG (self-hosted), Brave, TinyFish, Exa.
- **Ordered fallback chain**: a recoverable error (network, timeout, rate limit, bad response) moves to the next backend; a terminal one aborts; if all fail the error lists every attempt.
- **Keys without a restart**: the four key-backed backends are configured from the web client's Plugins page, written through the Host's credential store and resolved per request — never into a settings file, with environment variables as the fallback.
- **Boot-time chain**: the chain order, the SearXNG URL, the result cap, the timeout and the cache TTL are volatile fields set from your profile's patch layer (see [Configuration](#configuration)).

## Install

`lib/` is committed, so installing from GitHub needs no build step.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:orfeomorello/dsh-websearch-stack
```

To try on a disposable profile first:

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config > before.txt
dsh plugin --profile web add github:orfeomorello/dsh-websearch-stack
dsh --profile web --dump-config > after.txt
```

## Quick start

The default chain `['tavily', 'parallel-mcp']` works with **no key and no configuration**: Tavily runs keyless, Parallel needs no credentials. Install the plugin, restart the profile, and ask anything that needs current information — `web_search` answers through the chain.

From there:

- **want more or different sources?** reorder the chain or add a backend in the profile patch (see [Configuration](#configuration)) — SearXNG, Brave, TinyFish and Exa each need their own setup;
- **want your own instance?** follow [SearXNG](#searxng): no external API, no key, your infra;
- **want higher-quality Tavily results or Brave/Exa?** paste a key on the plugin's page in the web client; it takes effect on the next request.

## Configuration

Two surfaces, because the web client's Plugins page can only write credentials:

| What | Where | When it takes effect |
|---|---|---|
| API keys (`TAVILY_API_KEY`, `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`, `TINYFISH_API_KEY`, `EXA_API_KEY`) | the **Plugins page** → this bundle's page, through the settings card | the next request, no restart |
| `enabled_providers`, `searxng_url`, `default_max_results`, `default_timeout_ms`, `cache_ttl_seconds` | your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (or a `--patch` overlay) | at the next profile boot |

The second list is a host limitation, not a plugin one: in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager` 0.2.0-rc.2 the page renders `plugins.bundle.config` **without** a config form, so a bundle's own fields never get a widget. The fields are declared volatile (each one a reference the Host can rewrite in place), so a form written against `plugins.row.config` — or any CLI tooling that writes the namespace — would apply them live; today the profile patch is the way.

### Boot-time values

The values live in the profile's own patch layer, `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, keyed by this plugin's row id. This shape is verified with `dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config`:

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml
- id: websearch-stack
  name: dsh-websearch-stack
  config:
    enabled_providers: [tavily, parallel-mcp]
    default_max_results: 5
```

For a one-off try without touching the file, an overlay applied after every other layer:

```bash
dsh --profile web --patch ./searxng.yml
```

```yaml
# searxng.yml
- id: websearch-stack
  name: dsh-websearch-stack
  config:
    enabled_providers: [searxng, tavily]
    searxng_url: http://localhost:8080
```

An absent field keeps its default. An unknown value is refused by the schema, so a typo fails the boot instead of silently disabling a backend.

A Compose-style setup can keep the URL in the environment instead: the entry-list YAML dialect evaluates `!!js` scalars at entry activation, with Node globals in scope.

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml
- id: websearch-stack
  name: dsh-websearch-stack
  config:
    enabled_providers: [searxng, tavily]
    searxng_url: !!js process.env.SEARXNG_URL ?? ''
```

`--dump-config` prints the expression node unevaluated — the dump is the stored patch, not the resolved value.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled_providers` | `['tavily', 'parallel-mcp']` | Fallback chain, in order. Values: `tavily`, `parallel-mcp`, `searxng`, `brave`, `tinyfish`, `exa`. An empty list disables the plugin (see [How the fallback works](#how-the-fallback-works)). |
| `searxng_url` | — | Base URL of a self-hosted SearXNG instance, e.g. `http://localhost:8080`. Required for `searxng`. |
| `default_max_results` | `5` | Maximum sources per query when the request names none (1–20). |
| `default_timeout_ms` | `10000` | Per-backend request timeout in milliseconds (1 000–60 000). |
| `cache_ttl_seconds` | `60` | Cache TTL for identical queries. `0` disables the cache. |

### SearXNG

The self-hosted option: your instance, no external API, no key. It needs two things — an instance with the JSON format enabled, and `searxng_url` pointing at it.

1. Run an instance (Docker Compose, the project's recommended layout):

```bash
mkdir -p ./searxng/core-config/
cd ./searxng/
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/searxng/searxng/master/container/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/searxng/searxng/master/container/.env.example
cp -i .env.example .env
docker compose up -d
```

2. Enable the JSON format in `core-config/settings.yml` — `json` is **not** in the default `search.formats` (`html` only):

```yaml
search:
  formats:
    - html
    - json
```

3. Point the plugin at it (profile patch, then restart the profile):

```yaml
- id: websearch-stack
  name: dsh-websearch-stack
  config:
    enabled_providers: [searxng, tavily, parallel-mcp]
    searxng_url: http://localhost:8080
```

The backend calls `GET <searxng_url>/search?q=…&format=json&language=en` and reads `results[].{url,title,content}`. Without `searxng_url` the backend reports itself unavailable and the chain moves on. SearXNG's own installation details are in its [container](https://docs.searxng.org/admin/installation-docker.html) and [`search:` settings](https://docs.searxng.org/admin/settings/settings_search.html) pages.

## Backends

| Id | Key | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tavily` | `TAVILY_API_KEY` (optional) | Without a key sends `x-tavily-access-mode: keyless` (verified live). With a key, `Bearer`. |
| `parallel-mcp` | none | JSON-RPC `tools/call` on `web_search` (arguments `objective` and `search_queries`), no credentials. Verified live. |
| `searxng` | none | Self-hosted instance, requires `searxng_url`. Not verified (needs an instance). |
| `brave` | `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` | `X-Subscription-Token`. Not verified with a real key. |
| `tinyfish` | `TINYFISH_API_KEY` | `X-API-Key`. Not verified with a real key. |
| `exa` | `EXA_API_KEY` | `x-api-key`, `POST /search`. Not verified with a real key. |

Keys are read from the Host credential store, with the environment variables above as the fallback: a key written from the settings card is resolved per request, so it needs no environment export. The config YAML never holds secrets.

### Settings card (web client)

The plugin ships a configuration card for the dsh web client (`dsh.client.platform: "web"`). It appears on the **Plugins** page under the `dsh-websearch-stack` bundle and manages the four key-backed API keys through the Host's

# dsh-lead-panel

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-lead-panel)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-lead-panel)

## 关于「领导」模板：把 agent 当「人」用

> 这一节是作者的初衷，跟代码无关。
> 「领导 / 工人」是**本插件的用法比喻**；底下真正干活的那套团队机制是官方 Agent Teams
> （见下一节「官方能力 vs 本插件」）。

- 传统的 agent 主要用于**一次性对话**：做完这个「任务」后无法继续进行对话 ——
  这样很浪费 token，缓存命中率也白搭。
- 而「领导」这个模板把这些 agent 当作**单独的对话**使用，并且可以**相互通报、提交进度**。
- 这样子搞的话，到时候要修改，**直接让领导通知对应的（工人）模板**就行。
- 效果类似于（中国古代的）**「分封制」**：
  - 你是最高权力的**「老板」**，可以管理「领导」；
  - 「领导」管理「工人」，可以控制一切的选择和过程；
  - 而「领导」**永远不会控制「老板」**。
- 个人推荐：**「强模型」（领导）**把任务给**「次模型 / 本地模型」（工人）**
  （唯一的缺点可能就是速度问题）。
- 其实本质上就是**让 AI 管外包，但是有「领导」看着**：它可以实时地管理它们，
  甚至可以随时关掉它们 —— 防止出现**「层层外包」**这一情况。

### 三点说明

1. **关于总结**：领导会总结几个关键点用于简单说明（这方面主要给使用者看；
   如果你认为不行，可以让它对任务或者是计划进行修改）。
2. **目前无法切换创建后的（工人）「模型」**（如同上面说的）——
   面板上能切换的只是**领导自己**的模型；想换工人的模型，只能让它重新造一个。
3. **你可以不用「领导按钮」**（我也觉得这个没有用……）。
   按钮只是入口：领导会话说到底就是个普通 DSH 会话，在会话列表里直接打开它、
   跟它说话，效果一样；面板的价值只在于「看得见过程与花费」。

---

DSH 网页版的「领导面板」插件：在输入框的**「完全权限」右边**加一个 `领导` 按钮。
按下去弹出对话框，你和「领导」聊需求 —— 聊完让它总结并派活，运行期间实时显示
token、估算金额、用时和预计剩余时间。

当前版本 **0.5.2** ｜ [更新说明](RELEASE_NOTES.md) ｜ 自检 30 项 + Host 冒烟 29 项全过 ｜ 依赖官方 Agent Teams（实验性）

![DSH 领导面板](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/panel.png)

> 面板长这样：顶部是状态与**模型选择**（当前模型名 + provider 胶囊 + 推理强度），
> 中间是计划卡片、对话与工人区，底部是 token / 估算金额 / 用时 / 预计剩余 / 速度
> 五个指标块，以及「总结并派活」「发送」两个按钮。

## 它做什么

| 面板区域 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 顶部 | 领导当前状态（运行中 / 空闲）、**模型下拉框**（列出本机所有 provider/模型，按 provider 分组、模型全名、当前项打勾，选一下即切换），并常显当前模型 + provider 胶囊 + 推理强度；另有打断、重开 |
| 计划卡 | 领导总结的四段：`【需求】【效果】【分工】【预计时间】`，自动抽成卡片 |
| 中部 | 与领导的对话；助手消息下面挂它调用的工具名（`spawn_teammate` 等） |
| 工人区 | 领导派出去的工人 AI：名字、状态（running/inactive/provisioning/failed）、负责什么、各自的 token 与金额、最后一句结论 |
| 底部 | 实时指标块：`token / 估算金额 / 用时 / 预计剩余 / tok/s`，下面是输入框、「总结并派活」、「发送」 |

「总结并派活」会给领导一条固定指令：让它按四段回答，并立刻用 Agent Teams 的
`spawn_teammate` 把活派给工人 AI。

## 官方能力 vs 本插件（先说清楚）

> 一句话：**团队是官方的，这个插件是官方的「仪表盘 + 对讲机」。**

| 能力 | 提供方 |
|---|---|
| 团队协作；`spawn_teammate` / `send_message` / `team_task_*` / `list_agents` / `wait_agent` 等工具；成员名册；**共享任务看板**；DSH 自带的「智能体团队」面板 | **官方**（实验性功能，就是设置里那个「智能体团队」开关："启用团队协作、团队工具、成员列表和共享任务看板"） |
| 输入框旁的 `领导` 按钮；面板里的对话、**模型切换**、计划卡片、工人区、token / 估算金额 / 用时 / 预计剩余 | **本插件** |

本插件**不实现任何团队逻辑**：它只是建一个普通 DSH 会话当「领导」，把指令发给它，
再读官方的名册（`ctx.agentTeams.listMembers`）与用量投影，把过程显示出来。
代码里唯一出现 `spawn_teammate` 的地方，是**发给领导的指令文本**，不是它的实现。

**前置条件**：官方那个「智能体团队」开关必须打开，否则插件拿不到 `agentTeams` 服务，
「工人区」会是空的（面板会直接把原因显示出来）。

## 和官方的 Agent Teams 一起用

这个面板本质上是 Agent Teams 的「驾驶舱」：你只跟「领导」说话，造队友、派活、
收结果都由它自己完成（都是官方工具），而你在旁边看得见全过程。

### 1. 本地 AI 现场给你造队友

一句「你派几个子智能体来做」就够了 —— 领导自己起名字、定职责，用 `spawn_teammate`
把队友拉起来（下图里它自己造了「定位分析器 / 翻译 / 配置管理器」三个）：

![让本地 AI 直接创造智能体队友](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-spawn.png)

### 2. 队友之间互相汇报、统一推进

队友不是各干各的：它们能用 `send_message` 互发上下文与结论，领导再用
`wait_agent` 收口、`team_task_*` 协调分工，最后汇总成一份结果：

![智能体队友互相报告与统一推进](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-messaging.png)

### 3. 全队状态一目了然

DSH 自带的「智能体团队」面板列出每个成员与状态（谁是当前会话、谁在跑）：

![智能体团队面板](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-roster.png)

面板里的「工人」区块读的就是同一份名册（`ctx.agentTeams.listMembers`），
额外补上每个队友花掉的 token 与估算金额 —— 即使队友干完活被卸载了，
数字仍然从它的持久日志里折叠出来。

### 4. 队伍可以随着任务长大

人不够就继续造：下图是一支 8 人队伍 —— 一个 `lead` 加七个各管一段的工人
（本地化分析、翻译、配置管理、BepInEx 安装、构建、字符串提取、字体排查）：

![一支 8 人队伍](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-members8.png)

### 5. 派活不是发一段 prompt，而是开一张任务板

领导把活拆成带编号的共享任务（谁能写哪些文件、交付物是什么、验收标准是什么），
每个任务有 owner、有写入范围；成员名册与任务板就是它的施工图：

![成员与共享任务](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-taskboard.png)

### 6. 给工人的指令是一份交付规格，不是一句「你去做」

任务卡里写明目标、环境事实、步骤、交付物（可复用的脚本 + 报告），
甚至规定「严禁修改游戏目录内任何文件」这种边界：

![任务卡：目标 / 环境 / 步骤 / 交付物](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-task-brief.png)

连算法都写死到这种程度 —— 判据、保留规则、丢弃规则、去重、分类，
工人照着做就行，不需要它自己「发挥」：

![任务卡：算法与判据](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel/main/images/teams-task-spec.png)

这种「规格级」的派活方式正是「领导」模板的价值：**决策留在领导，执行交给工人**，
出问题时能一眼看出是哪一层的责任。

## 安装

```powershell
# 从 npm 安装（推荐）
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-lead-panel

# 从 GitHub 安装（想跟 main 分支最新代码走就用这条）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mutoharohfiqhiabcd-source/dsh-lead-panel

# 从本地目录安装
dsh plugin --profile web add D:\1231\dsh-lead-panel

# 或者手工：把本目录复制到 <DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-lead-panel，
# 再往 <DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\cordis.patch.yml 追加：
#
#    - insert:
#        - id: dsh-lead-panel
#          name: dsh-lead-panel
```

npm 包：<https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-lead-panel>（MIT）—— 几种装法装的是同一份
代码，装完都要**重启 DSH** 才会加载 Host 半边。

`patchReload: live` 的 profile 会在 patch 变化时热重载；否则重启 DSH。
（注意：改 Host 代码后 DSH 会复用已缓存的模块，见文末「改代码时的两个坑」。）

## 配置（profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 里覆盖该行 config）

```yaml
- id: dsh-lead-panel
  config:
    title: 领导                 # 领导会话标题
    cwd: D:\1231                # 领导会话的工作目录
    leadPreset: standard        # 领导会话用哪个 agent preset
    leadModel: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-flash }
    currency: '¥'
    prices:                     # 元 / 百万 token，覆盖内置牌价
      deepseek-flash: { input: 2, cacheRead: 0.2, output: 3 }
```

## 接口（Host 半边，只允许本机访问）

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/lead-panel/api/state` | 面板轮询：消息 / 计划 / 工人 / 用量 / 模型清单 |
| GET | `/lead-panel/api/health` | 自检：Host 服务可用性、状态文件位置、build 标记 |
| GET | `/lead-panel/api/debug-session?id=<会话id>` | 排查：直接读某个会话的持久日志，看能不能算出用量 |
| POST | `/lead-panel/api/ensure` | 确保领导会话存在（`{reset:true}` 重开） |
| POST | `/lead-panel/api/send` | `{text}` 给领导发消息 |
| POST | `/lead-panel/api/dispatch` | `{text}` 总结并派活 |
| POST | `/lead-panel/api/model` | `{provider, model}` 切换领导模型 |
| POST | `/lead-panel/api/cancel` | 打断领导当前回合 |

领导会话的 id 存在 `<DSH_HOME>\lead-panel\state.json`，重启 DSH 后复用同一个会话。

## 自检

```powershell
npm test                  # 两个套件一起跑
node test/self-check.mjs  # 30 项：纯逻辑 + 浏览器半边
node test/host-smoke.mjs  # 29 项：假 ctx 把 Host 的 HTTP 链路整条跑一遍
```

- `self-check`：用量折叠、金额折算、计划抽取、消息过滤、价目表覆盖；以及在假
  `window.__ModuleLoader__` + 假 `react` 下求值 `lib/client.js`，确认它注册到
  `conversation.input.left`、组件可构造、防翻译标记在位。
- `host-smoke`：用假 ctx / 假服务驱动真实处理器，验证 `POST /send`、`/dispatch`
  会给 `sessionController.prompt` 传 `AbortSignal`（曾经漏传，面板点了报
  `throwIfAborted`）、`/state` 能抽出计划卡片与工人用量（含已卸载工人读持久日志）、
  金额按牌价折算、异常以 JSON 返回。

两套都不依赖 DSH，改完先跑。

## 说明与边界

- **团队能力来自官方，不是本插件**：成员名册、共享任务看板、`spawn_teammate` 等工具都由
  官方 Agent Teams（实验性）提供；本插件只读它们、并把过程显示出来 + 提供模型切换与派活入口。
  官方开关关掉时，插件只剩「和领导的对话」与用量显示。
- **金额是估算**：DSH 本身只有 token 计数、没有金额模型，所以插件内置一张 DeepSeek
  牌价表（元/百万 token），按 `未命中输入 / 命中输入 / 输出` 三个桶折算；牌价变了改配置即可。
- **预计剩余时间也是估算**：没有历史时长库，用「已完成工人数 × 已用时长」外推；
  工人还没跑完一个时显示「估算中…」。领导在计划里自己给的预计时间会出现在对话正文里。
- 面板依赖 Host 服务 `sessionController`（建会话/发消息/切模型）、`sessionProjections`
  （实时用量）与 `agentTeams`（工人名册）；缺哪个就在面板上显示对应的错误，不会影响
  DSH 其它功能。工人干完活会被卸载，插件改读它的**持久日志**折叠 token，所以 settle
  之后仍然能看到它花了多少。

## 改代码时的两个坑（实测）

1. **Host 模块按 package.json 的 `name` 缓存。** 改了 `index.js` 后，即使把 profile 的
   `cordis.patch.yml` 里那一行删掉再加回来，DSH 仍然跑旧代码。要么换一个没用过的包名
   （目录名 + `package.json` 的 `name` 一起改），要么重启 DSH。
2. **不要用脚本（PowerShell 等）去改写 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`。** 实测一次
   `Get-Content -Raw | Set-Content` 往返会把中文注释行拼成一行，把后面的
   `- id:` / `- insert:` 吞进注释里，于是整段配置静默失效；更糟的是，反复替换这个文件
   会让 DSH 的文件监听器失效，之后**任何** patch 改动（连最小 canary 插件）都不再热加载，
   只能重启 DSH。改这个文件请用编辑器逐行改。

plugins.description: Go (圍棋) plugin for the DeepSeek Harness: full rules engine, three-level AI, dead-stone estimator, LLM review, SGF, and an optional KataGo GTP bridge
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-go-game

圍棋 for the DeepSeek Harness. A full rules engine, a three-level AI partner,
a playout dead-stone estimator, optional LLM review, SGF save/load — surfaced
both as a DSH panel (`shell.overlay`) and as a standalone page at
`/dsh-go-game/`.

## What it does

**Rules (host half, pure JS).** 19×19 / 13×13 / 9×9, Chinese area scoring
(stones + surrounded empty points), configurable komi and handicap, capture by
liberty exhaustion, no suicide, simple ko (immediate recapture forbidden),
pass / two-pass end, resignation, unlimited undo, SGF import and export.
Dead-stone adjudication is explicit: both sides pass, dead stones are marked
(manually or by the estimator), then the area is counted.

**The AI.** Three levels, all run in the host process:

| level | how it plays |
| --- | --- |
| `easy` 入門 | random legal moves that avoid filling its own eyes |
| `medium` 中級 | greedy tactics: capture, rescue from atari, atari the opponent, shape/line preference |
| `hard` 進階 | the medium candidate list, each scored by light random playouts inside a wall-clock budget |

**Honest limit:** this is a practice partner, not an engine. On 19×19 even
`hard` is far below a human amateur; on 9×9 it plays a recognisable game.

**Dead-stone estimator.** `形勢判斷` runs random playouts (avoiding own-eye
fills) from the current position and reports which stones rarely survive, plus a
per-point ownership map the board renders as a translucent overlay. It is an
estimate, not an adjudication — correct anything it gets wrong with `標記死子`.

**LLM review (optional).** `覆盤` asks the harness `llm` service (no API keys in
this plugin) for a short Cantonese commentary plus a suggested move, which the
panel offers as a one-click play. Without a configured model it degrades to the
local scoring summary.

## Layout

| file | face | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/engine.js` | shared | rules: board, capture, ko, score, SGF — no DOM, no DSH imports |
| `lib/ai.js` | host | heuristics, playout opponent, dead-stone estimator |
| `lib/gtp.js` | host | GTP bridge to an external neural-network engine (KataGo) |
| `lib/index.js` | host | sessions + every `/dsh-go-game/*` route, LLM review, SGF files |
| `lib/client.js` | web | the React panel registered in `shell.overlay` |
| `lib/page.html`, `lib/page.js` | web | the standalone page (a thin view over the same routes) |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | — | inserts the plugin row into the web profile roster |
| `test/*.test.mjs` | — | 98 cases: 26 engine, 11 AI, 22 host routes, 26 GTP, 13 engine fallback |
| `check-plugin.ps1` / `.cmd` | — | read-only install check |

No rules live in the browser: both views post intent and re-render the state the
host returns.

## Tests

```
node test/engine.test.mjs
node test/ai.test.mjs
node test/host.test.mjs
node test/gtp.test.mjs             # GTP bridge, driven by an injected fake engine
node test/engine-fallback.test.mjs # engine selected but absent -> built-in AI
node test/katago-live.mjs --root=<katago dir>   # real engine, skipped without --root
```

Run each file directly; `node --test` fails on this machine (the runner spawns a
piped child process and the sandbox rejects it). The host suite drives the real
routes through a mock webserver, mock `req`/`res` and a mock `llm`, so the whole
non-UI chain is covered offline.

## KataGo (optional neural-network opponent)

`lib/ai.js` is a heuristic/playout practice partner. For real strength,
`lib/gtp.js` drives an external KataGo process over GTP, **side by side** with the
built-in AI: the panel's `引擎` selector picks one per game, and a missing or
broken engine falls back to the built-in opponent automatically (the reason is
shown in the panel, not swallowed).

Layout it looks for (relative to the workspace, i.e. one level above the plugin):

```
katago/engine/katago.exe        Eigen (CPU) build, or any other backend
katago/engine/default_gtp.cfg   optional, ships with the release
katago/weights/*.bin.gz         one or more networks
```

Environment overrides:

| variable | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_ROOT` | `<plugin>/../../katago` | engine + weights root |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_THREADS` | 4 | search threads (stay below the core count) |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_VISITS` | 250 | hard visit ceiling per move |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_TIME` | 8 | **seconds per move** — bounds CPU latency |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_TIMEOUT` | 90000 | GTP command timeout (ms) |

`GET /dsh-go-game/engine` reports availability, the network list and live status;
`POST /dsh-go-game/engine {model:"<file>"}` switches network, restarting the
process (KataGo loads exactly one network at startup).

Measured on this machine — i5-8250U, 4 threads, no GPU, b18c384 on the AVX2 Eigen
build: first move ≈ 11 s (it loads the 93 MB network), later moves ≈ 8 s with
`maxTime=8`. Because the search is time-bounded, slower hardware loses strength
rather than latency. Every query replays the game onto a clean engine board after
an explicit `clear_board`: KataGo does *not* wipe the stones on a same-size
`boardsize`, which otherwise surfaces as a spurious "illegal move".

## Install (three steps, outside DSH)

The agent sandbox cannot write outside the workspace, so profile registration is
a manual step — run these in a normal terminal:

1. In the active profile `package.json` (`%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web`):
   add `"dsh-go-game": "link:C:/AppDev/DSH_WORKSPACE/dsh-go-game"` to
   `dependencies`, and append `"dsh-go-game"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`.
2. Point node_modules at the source directory (DSH does not run `pnpm install`
   on boot, and a missing link fails silently):

   ```
   mklink /J "%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-go-game" "C:\AppDev\DSH_WORKSPACE\dsh-go-game"
   ```

3. Restart DSH.

`check-plugin.cmd` verifies all four links of the chain (package → registration →
node_modules → live route) at any point.

Routes are unauthenticated on loopback, matching the other local plugins:
`GET /dsh-go-game/status` answering JSON is the fastest proof of life.

## Notes and unverified parts

- Sessions live in host memory (12-hour idle sweep) and are keyed by a client id
  the panel/page generates; restarting DSH clears them. SGF files persist under
  `<workspace>/.dsh-go-game/games/`.
- The playout estimator is CPU-bound by design and budget-limited (default
  1500 ms, 40 playouts). It runs on the host so the panel never blocks.
- **Not yet verified on a live GUI**: the panel's rendering inside
  `shell.overlay`, its pointer-event behaviour, and the LLM review path against a
  real provider. The engine, AI and every route are covered by the offline
  suites.

# dsh-restart-hotkey

> **DSH (DeepSeek Harness) 桌面端快捷键重启插件**  
> 一键自定义快捷键极速重启 DSH 桌面端，支持防误触二次确认弹窗、动态按键录制、通用设置面板集成与进程安全拉起机制。

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-DSH%20Desktop%20%7C%20Windows-green.svg)](#)

---

## ✨ 功能特性

1. **安全稳定的应用无缝平滑重启**：
   - 彻底关闭原有 Electron 主进程及所有常驻子进程，并在释放系统句柄与端口锁定后通过 Windows Shell 独立拉起全新的 `DeepSeek Harness.exe`，避免父子进程生命周期锁定问题。
2. **应用内专属生效**：
   - 仅在 DSH 窗口处于激活前台焦点状态时捕获按键，绝不与系统其他全局热键或常用软件冲突。
3. **支持完全自定义快捷键（默认 `Ctrl+Shift+R`）**：
   - 支持在设置页面中自由录制，支持鼠标点击后**直接敲击键盘组合键自动录制**，无需手动输入繁琐的键名。
   - 提供常用预设一键切换（`Ctrl+Shift+R`、`Alt+R`、`F9`、`Ctrl+Alt+R`）。
4. **防误触二次确认弹窗**：
   - 按下快捷键时弹出优雅的确认对话框，提供“确认重启 (Enter)”与“取消 (Esc)”。
   - 支持直接勾选“下次直接重启，无需确认”，亦可在弹窗底部直接点击“更改快捷键”完成按键重绑。
5. **多处无缝设置入口**：
   - **【设置】→【通用】页面**：在 DSH 默认的通用偏好列表中直接嵌入配置行，开箱即可调配。
   - **【设置】左侧导航独立页面**：提供专属的独立卡片设置界面。
   - **【插件】→【配置】**：与 DSH 插件管理生态全面对齐。

---

## 🛠️ 安装方法

### 方式一：目录链接安装（推荐开发调试）
1. 将本项目 clone 或解压到本地目录（如 `C:\Users\<YourUser>\Documents\DSH\dsh-plugin\dsh-restart-hotkey`）。
2. 打开 **DSH 桌面端 → 左侧栏「插件」→「安装插件」**。
3. 填入插件项目目录的绝对路径，点击安装。
4. 安装完成后重启 DSH 即可生效。

### 方式二：打包安装 (npm pack)
在项目根目录下打包：
```bash
npm pack
```
在 **DSH 桌面端 →「插件」→「安装」** 中填入生成的 `.tgz` 压缩包路径即可。

---

## ⚙️ 快捷键与配置项

进入 **DSH【设置】→【通用】** 或 **【快捷重启】**：

| 配置项 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **重启快捷键** (`hotkey`) | `Ctrl+Shift+R` | 点击“录制按键”后直接敲击键盘组合键自动保存，亦可使用内置预设 |
| **重启前弹窗二次确认** (`confirmBeforeRestart`) | `true` | 开启后按下快捷键先弹出确认模态框；关闭后按下快捷键将立即直接重启 |
| **测试重启应用** | - | 点击可立即模拟执行一次平滑重启过程，用于验证运行状态 |

---

## 🧪 自动化测试验证

本项目自带完备的单元测试，涵盖快捷键解析、规范化比对、按键匹配算法、进程路径识别与 Cordis 契约验证：

```bash
node test/hotkey.test.mjs
node test/restart.test.mjs
node test/plugin-wiring.test.mjs
```

---

## 📄 开源协议

本项目采用 [MIT](LICENSE) 协议开源。

# dsh-knowspace

**Agent-native, local-first knowledge infrastructure for DeepSeekHarness.**

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README_zh.md)

> **Status: Work in progress · Public placeholder · No public alpha release**  
> Last README update: October 12, 2026. Development continues in a private repository. This public repository currently serves as the project's official landing page; it does not provide an installable plugin or publicly auditable source code.

`dsh-knowspace` aims to make personal knowledge available to both people and authorized AI agents without making a cloud service, a vector database, or an always-on AI process the owner of that knowledge. It is designed as a [DeepSeekHarness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin, not a separate knowledge server.

The long-term goal is a shared foundation for notes, retrieval, rendering, and interaction that other agents, Skills, scripts, and domain-specific plugins can reuse.

## Why KnowSpace?

Most AI workflows treat knowledge as one-off chat context or an external retrieval service. KnowSpace takes a different approach:

- **Your files are the source of truth.** Markdown notes and images remain ordinary, portable local assets.
- **Agents work within permissions.** Access is scoped by workspace and user policy; knowledge is not silently exposed to every agent.
- **Offline comes first.** Reading, editing, and baseline search should work without network access.
- **Sync is optional.** A WebDAV endpoint can exchange supported knowledge assets between devices without hosting a separate KnowSpace service.
- **Interactive content is reusable infrastructure.** Math rendering, diagrams, temporary pages, and input collection belong in common capabilities rather than being reinvented by every Skill.

**Design principle:** Your knowledge, your control. AI participation should be explicit, scoped, and reviewable.

## Project status

The first five internal development rounds have been recorded as closed in the private project's progress history. **This is not equivalent to completing public release acceptance.** Some implementation results have been reported internally, while important security, synchronization, and end-to-end checks remain part of the acceptance plan.

| Area | Current description | Public availability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeekHarness Host/Client integration and sidebar | Implemented in private development records; compatibility is version-sensitive | Not released |
| Local workspaces, Markdown, JPG/PNG assets, basic search | Implemented/reported internally; subject to regression checks | Not released |
| Agent knowledge tools, edits, and change previews | Implemented/reported internally; end-to-end gateway checks are tracked separately | Not released |
| Markdown and mathematical notation | Existing private implementation and test history; maintained rather than rewritten | Not released |
| WebDAV bidirectional synchronization | Designed and worked on internally; cross-device/conflict/data-safety evidence must satisfy release gates | Not released |
| Interactive HTML, drawing input, submission bridge | Partially implemented or planned; security sandbox and real UI flows are not yet fully accepted | Not released |
| Editable knowledge diagrams and advanced local retrieval | Architecture decisions made; integration and acceptance are pending | Not released |

**No installation instructions are published yet.** A pinned, reproducible installation process and compatibility matrix will accompany the first usable alpha release. Please do not treat a development design or an example tool name as a supported public API.

## Product capabilities and direction

### 1. Knowledge: workspaces, files, and optional sync

Two intended workspace modes keep their responsibilities separate:

| Workspace | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Local** | Independent knowledge workspace stored on the current device; never synced automatically. |
| **Synced** | Complete local working copy with optional, bidirectional WebDAV synchronization when connectivity is available. |

Markdown is the primary portable knowledge format. The default **sync allowlist** is `.md`, `.jpg`, and `.png`; PDF, video, audio, 3D files, executable content, and native diagram sources are not automatically uploaded as originals. Rich media may remain local. A Markdown document explicitly derived from rich media is an independent knowledge asset, not a continuously attached copy of its source.

The design prioritizes change history, understandable diffs, collision protection, non-destructive conflict handling, and recovery over silent overwrites.

### 2. Retrieval: local-first search and evidence

KnowSpace starts with workspace-aware textual retrieval. Its planned search improvements borrow *ideas* from Greb-style candidate retrieval and ranking, but **do not use a cloud Greb API or make any third-party MCP service mandatory**.

The intended retrieval path is:

```text
Authorized workspaces
        |
Local text / file candidates
        |
Filtering + ranking / optional fusion
        |
Traceable source passages
        |
Agent answer or user-facing search result
```

Optional local accelerators such as ripgrep or SQLite FTS5 may be used when compatible. In-process scanning remains the fallback. Embeddings and reranking are optional later extensions, not prerequisites for a useful knowledge library.

### 3. Rendering: Markdown, math, and safe previews

The shared rendering layer is intended to support:

- Markdown notes, tables, code blocks, and image references.
- LaTeX-style mathematical expressions and math-friendly study material.
- Safe, bounded previews of knowledge content and tool results.
- Temporary interactive artifacts where the Host can enforce isolation, permissions, and resource limits.

Untrusted HTML/JavaScript must not gain access to the Host, filesystem, or agent permissions merely because it is displayed in a note or preview. Interactive execution is gated separately from Markdown rendering.

### 4. Interaction: agent-to-user workflows

Beyond static reading, KnowSpace is being designed to support explicit agent-created interaction flows: a temporary page or form is shown to the user, the user submits structured input or an image, and the authorized agent receives that result through a controlled bridge.

Examples include handwritten mathematical answers, study exercises, research review forms, and Skill-generated visual tools. These are examples of reusable infrastructure, **not a promise that a full exam platform or research product is included in the core plugin**.

### 5. Knowledge diagrams: editable diagrams rather than image generation

A planned diagram capability will represent flowcharts, mind maps, and system architecture diagrams as **editable vector/structured assets**, rather than requiring photorealistic image-generation models.

The selected approach is to selectively adapt suitable `.drawio` parsing, model, and layout concepts/code from [fourzkw/dsh-drawai](https://github.com/fourzkw/dsh-drawai), subject to pinned-source and license review. Host authorization, workspace handling, and agent tools remain owned by KnowSpace. The native editable `.drawio` source is local-only by default; an explicitly exported `.png` can be stored as a separate knowledge asset under the normal sync policy.

**This diagram integration has been designed, not shipped.**

## Intended architecture

```text
DeepSeekHarness
  |-- Sidebar / knowledge UI
  |-- Agent tools (scoped operations)
  |-- Skills and other plugins
  |
  `-- dsh-knowspace plugin
       |-- Knowledge Core: workspaces / assets / changes / access
       |-- Retrieval Core: local search / source evidence
       |-- Rendering Core: Markdown / math / safe previews
       |-- Interaction Core: temporary artifacts / user submissions
       |-- Diagram capability: editable structured assets (planned)
       |
       |-- Local filesystem and indexes
       `-- Optional WebDAV synchronization (allowlisted files)

No dedicated KnowSpace server or mandatory cloud vector database.
```

This diagram describes the **target architecture**, not
