plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-squares

[**English**](README.md) | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

An **all-in-one workspace plugin** for DSH (DeepSeek Harness): it adds a global
「Square」panel to the Web GUI sidebar that manages **Skills / Experts / Connectors (MCP) / Plugins**
in a single place. **Web (`dsh web`) and Desktop (DeepSeek Harness.app) share the same code and build output.**

Sidebar → 「Square」panel: the four tabs show the Square (official/community catalog) by default; the
「My Experts / My Skills / My MCP / My Plugins」items in the top-right open sub-pages to manage local
content, and 「Back to Square」at the top of the sub-page returns to the Square.

## 1. Installation

Published on npm and GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-squares            # install from npm
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ai-tool-labs/dsh-squares   # or from GitHub
# Desktop: open the "Plugins" panel in the sidebar → click "Add Plugin" → type "dsh-squares" → Install
# Restart harness after installing to take effect (Desktop: restart the App; Web: restart dsh web)
```

A 「Square」entry then appears in the sidebar; click it to open the panel.

## 2. Screenshots

The **Square** panel as it appears in the Web GUI sidebar:

![Square example](assets/example/example-01.png)

## 3. Development

```bash
pnpm --filter dsh-squares typecheck    # host + client tsconfigs
pnpm --filter dsh-squares build        # tsc(host) + tsc(client .d.ts) + esbuild bundle
pnpm --filter dsh-squares smoke        # host smoke test (real Cordis lifecycle + filesystem + routes)
pnpm --filter dsh-squares test:routes  # route integration (expert/connector write paths)
pnpm --filter dsh-squares check:client # bundle shape / id / external-dependency allowlist + mock loader
```

### Building and installing from source (developer)

```bash
pnpm --filter dsh-squares build                                 # build (run pnpm install in the workspace first)
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/dsh-squares    # 2A) Web profile
# 2B) Desktop: the profile is exclusively owned by Electron; use a relative path to write it into the manifest and link via pnpm
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
d.setdefault('dependencies', {})['dsh-squares'] = 'link:/absolute/path/packages/dsh-squares'
bundles = d['dsh']['profile']['bundles']
if 'dsh-squares' not in bundles:
    bundles.append('dsh-squares')
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2) + '\n')
PY
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && CI=true pnpm install
# 3) Restart harness (Desktop: reopen the App; Web: restart dsh web)
```

plugins.description: An unofficial MIT-licensed image and video wallpaper plugin for DeepSeek Harness, with frosted UI panels, opacity controls and visual presets.
plugins.readme_text:
[English](README.en.md) | [简体中文](README.md)

> **Unofficial third-party plugin. Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.**

# DSH Wallpaper / DSH 壁纸背景

> **v0.3.0-rc.7 — MIT-licensed preview candidate; Desktop visual acceptance pending.** A local image/video wallpaper plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Desktop and Web. This changes **only the DSH app window**, not the OS desktop wallpaper. Licensed under **MIT**; publication and Desktop acceptance are still pending.

## ✨ 功能

- **壁纸**：静态 PNG/JPG/WebP，及 Chromium 支持的视频格式（推荐 H.264 MP4/WebM）；本地导入、循环静音播放、独立记忆两种文件。
- **独立设置分类**：`设置 → 壁纸背景`，与「通用」平级，中英文界面。
- **分区透明度（本版本新增）**：四个滑块分别控制「聊天正文」「左侧栏」「顶部导航」「输入框」的**底色不透明度**，互不连动。不会降低整张壁纸的透明度，也不会调节文字透明度。
-  **双模糊调节**：原「模糊」更名为「壁纸自身模糊」（覆盖壁纸的独立 `backdrop-filter` 层，不改变图像尺寸），另加「面板磨砂强度」（`backdrop-filter`，只采样面板后面的壁纸，不模糊面板内文字）。壁纸不透明度、暗度、铺满/完整显示、暂停与系统减少动态效果均保留。
- **侧栏修复**：壁纸启用时消除工作区会话列表底部的白色渐隐遮挡及硬截断线，保留滚动与较柔和的滚动条。
- **可恢复性**：壁纸关闭时自动撤销样式；提供「恢复推荐透明度」、测试渐变图案与诊断信息。
- **外观预设（rc.7 重新设计）**：阅读强调清晰内容、均衡强调半透明玻璃、沉浸强调完整壁纸；三套预设一键应用；支持另存最多 12 个命名自定义预设、覆盖更新和确认后删除。
- **实时 A/B 对比（rc.4）**：拖动滑块时立即更新并保存；自动保存首次调整前的临时比较基准，同时提供双缩略示意图、主窗口切换「修改前 / 当前」和一键恢复。切换查看本身不写入设置。
- **本地隐私**：壁纸 Blob 存入当前客户端 IndexedDB，外观偏好与自定义预设存入不同的 `localStorage` 键。插件不向远端上传壁纸或预设。

## 🎚️ 预设、对比与“透明度”语义

**术语统一**：本插件控制的是壁纸和 UI 面板的**不透明度（opacity）**，不是透明度（transparency）。两者数学上相反：`透明度 = 100% - 不透明度`。例如壁纸**不透明度 40%**意味着只保留 40% 的壁纸像素贡献（在普通 Alpha 叠加模型下），**不是**壁纸有 40% 的透明程度。0% 面板底色不透明度＝底板透明；100%＝底板不透明；滑块不会改变文字自身的不透明度。

**升级安全**：此前设置页错把 `opacity` 显示为「壁纸透明度」。rc.4 **只改标签、不反转数值**，原来存储的 40% 更新后依然是 40%，效果不突变；`localStorage` 媒体偏好键保持 `dsh-local-video-wallpaper-prefs-v2`。壁纸不透明度范围仍为 15%–100%。

### 一键预设

- **阅读**：壁纸柔和失焦，内容区底色更接近不透明，适合长时间阅读。
- **均衡**：更清楚的壁纸 + 局部磨砂玻璃，以交互和氛围平衡为目标。
- **沉浸**：完整清晰的壁纸、显著降低界面底色与去除磨砂，复杂图片上应注意文字对比度。
- **自定义**：输入名称后「另存为新预设」；选中已保存的预设后可「更新选中预设」或二次确认删除。最多 12 个，留在当前设备本地，不同步，不存储实际壁纸文件。

应用预设只改变 9 项外观参数（暗度、壁纸模糊、面板磨砂、壁纸不透明度、四个分区不透明度和适配模式），**不会**自动切换壁纸模式、替换文件、改变暂停或减少动态效果。升级不自动应用任何预设，也不覆盖用户之前的配置。

### 比较与一键恢复

修改滑块/应用预设时，插件自动记录第一笔修改之前的 9 项外观值作为 A；当前已保存外观作为 B。两张缩略示意图使用同一图片/视频来源及模拟 UI 底板，不渲染任何聊天记录；视频缩略图不自动播放，因此**以主窗口实效为准**。可点「主窗口查看修改前」「主窗口查看当前」临时切换实际背景；**查看 A 不会写回持久化设置，滑块始终显示 B**。点「一键恢复修改前」才真正恢复 A 并保存，点「结束对比（保留当前）」则放弃临时基准而保留 B。可以随时「以当前效果重新设为基准」。关闭/重启 DSH 后对比快照消失，自定义预设和当前滑块仍然保留。

详细规则见 [预设与对比设计](docs/PRESETS.md)、[三档视觉差异设计](docs/PRESET-DESIGN.md)。此外，DSH 官方插件管理页也使用“聊天正文”的底色不透明度作为内容底板，以避免插件列表中的文字直接压在壁纸上。

## 🎛️ 分区透明度

| 区域 / Region | 默认不透明度 | 调节的界面部分 |
|---|---:|---|
| 聊天正文 / Conversation body | 35% | 聊天内容阅读底板；不覆盖顶部导航 |
| 左侧栏 / Left sidebar | 90% | 整个侧栏底板，防止文字和图标被壁纸干扰 |
| 顶部导航 / Top navigation | 35% | 对话内标题与 View 标签；**不包含 Windows/macOS 原生标题栏菜单** |
| 输入框 / Composer input | 94% | 可输入文字的卡片；保留原有边框、阴影与交互 |

> **原有设置安全迁移**：更新 v0.2.x 时，「聊天正文」与「顶部导航」先继承旧「界面底色覆盖」（`tint`）的数值；侧栏默认 90%，输入框默认 94%，尽量保持可读性。所有媒体、暗度、模糊与壁纸透明度不变。旧 `tint` 数据保留用于降级兼容；新版不再展示旧全局遮罩滑块。

调整范围 0%–100%。0% 表示该区域底色完全透明，100% 表示该区域的底色不透明（壁纸仍保留在背景层）。建议先将**壁纸不透明度**设为 70%–100%，再按需增减阅读区域底色。过低的不透明度会降低可读性。

分区不透明度并非全局主题系统：**官方插件管理页额外使用聊天正文底色不透明度**，右侧第三方插件面板、弹窗和原生 Desktop 标题栏不会随这四个滑块改变。主聊天底部的原有渐变淡出与「聊天正文」透明度联动，不属于输入卡片本身。详细设计见 [docs/REGION-OPACITY.md](docs/REGION-OPACITY.md)。

## 🧊 壁纸模糊 vs 面板磨砂（v0.3.0-rc.3）

| 参数 | 生效位置 | 范围 | 升级后默认 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 壁纸自身模糊（旧 `blur`） | 壁纸图片 / 视频画面本身 | 0–20px | 继承旧值 |
| 面板磨砂强度（新 `panelBlur`） | 侧栏底板、对话正文底板、顶部导航、输入卡片的背景像素 | 0–12px | **0px**（不增加磨砂） |

**建议的“壁纸细节清晰、文字背后磨砂”设置**：壁纸自身模糊 **0px**、面板磨砂 **4–6px**，聊天正文不透明度约 **30–50%**、输入框 90–95%。侧栏若高于 90% 不透明，磨砂变化可能不明显。提高面板磨砂不会降低 UI 字体清晰度，但可能增加动态视频的 GPU 合成负担；低性能设备先使用 2–4px 或关闭。

实现使用 Chrome/Electron 的 `backdrop-filter` 与 `-webkit-backdrop-filter`，只在磨砂值大于 0 时注入相关 CSS；切换到关闭壁纸模式后释放该样式。磨砂会应用在 UI 的四个区域上；**输入卡片位于正文内部，局部磨砂可能发生叠加**，效果仍需真实 Desktop 验证。

**壁纸模糊不再放大（rc.6）**：壁纸画面在 0px、1px、4px 和 20px 模糊时保持相同的尺寸、铺满/适应方式和裁剪位置。模糊由覆盖在壁纸上的透明背景模糊层负责，不对图片/视频进行 `scale()`。这避免了 0px → 1px 的构图跳变以及单纯移除缩放时的浅色边缘。对比预览同步采用此方案，视频不增加第二路解码。高模糊可能增加 GPU 合成开销，可按设备性能降低模糊值。

**Windows 兼容修复（始于 rc.5，rc.6 保留）**：侧栏磨砂已改由独立的 `::before` 背景层绘制，不再把 `backdrop-filter` 加在侧栏容器本身。此前这样会让 `position:fixed` 的折叠按钮相对侧栏定位，向下移动并覆盖 DeepSeek Logo。设置 0px 与 6px 时折叠按钮应保持原位；新的 Chromium 回归检查已验证该定位关系，真实 Desktop 仍需确认。

## 📥 安装与更新

> **当前仍为私有预发布候选版。** 以下 Git tag 安装地址将在维护者创建 `v0.3.0-rc.7` 标签、仓库允许目标用户访问后可用；目前**尚未创建 tag，也没有公开 GitHub Release**。优先使用私有测试用的本地 `.tgz` 或源码目录验收。

**方式 A：从 GitHub 固定版本安装（推荐用于发布后）**

在 DSH **插件 → 添加插件** 中输入以下 Git 源（也可通过 CLI 安装到对应的 profile）：

```text
github:deepseaandhighsky-arch/DSH-Wallpaper#v0.3.0-rc.7
```

官方建议对来源敏感的 Git 安装固定**提交 SHA**；固定 tag 方便阅读与升级，但 tag 本身理论上可以被重写。仓库还是 Private 时，安装端必须拥有相应的 Git 访问权限。

**方式 B：通过 `.tgz` 文件安装（无需 Git 访问，适合普通用户）**

从未来的 GitHub Pre-release 下载 `local-dsh-video-wallpaper-0.3.0-rc.7.tgz`，在 **插件 → 添加插件** 中选择本地压缩包或输入其绝对路径；也可在 CLI 中使用 `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./local-dsh-video-wallpaper-0.3.0-rc.7.tgz`（在安装包所在目录执行）。**不要解压 `.tgz` 再安装**。发布前，维护者可从 GitHub Actions 的 `wallpaper-candidate-tgz` 测试工件获取它；该工件不是正式 Release，且仅短期保留。

**方式 C：源码目录（开发与排障）**

下载完整仓库（必须有 `package.json`、`index.js`、`client.js`、`cordis.patch.yml`），通过 DSH Creator Mode 的 `plugin_manager install_bundle`，将 `target` 指向仓库目录绝对路径。安装后从系统托盘**彻底退出 DSH Desktop 并重启**，前往 **设置 → 壁纸背景**确认版本 `0.3.0-rc.7`；先使用测试图案，再导入个人媒体。

详见 [安装说明](docs/INSTALLATION.md) / [English quick start](README.en.md) / [故障排查](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)。现阶段包名 `@local/dsh-video-wallpaper` **未发布到 npm**，勿把它当作 npm 注册表包名安装。不要清空 DSH Profile：媒体位于该 Profile 的浏览器存储内。

## 🧪 开发与验证

Requirements: Node.js 22+（使用原生测试运行器，无需额外 npm 依赖）。

```bash
npm run check           # 语法检查、数据与源码回归测试
npm run pack:tgz        # 生成并校验官方兼容的 .tgz + SHA-256（不会发布到 npm）
npm run visual:smoke    # 可选：需要独立可运行的 Chromium（可通过 CHROME_BIN 指定）
```

`visual:smoke` 使用仿照官方 DOM 结构的**独立静态页面**来检查 CSS 计算结果。它不是 DSH Electron 实机端到端测试，部分容器会无法启动 Chromium。**目前已完成 Node 测试，真实 DSH Desktop 的新版视觉验收仍在进行。**

## 📘 项目文档

- [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) · [当前状态](PROJECT-STATUS.md) · [待办路线图](docs/ROADMAP.md)
- [三档预设设计](docs/PRESET-DESIGN.md) · [分区透明度与磨砂设计](docs/REGION-OPACITY.md) · [安装说明](docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [故障排查](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)
- [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [安全政策](SECURITY.md)

## ⚠️ 已知限制

- 官方当前没有专用 `shell.background` 插件 Slot；背景依旧使用 `shell.overlay` + Portal。若 DSH 调整布局，部分区域可能需要重新适配。
- Chrome/Electron 视频解码和 IndexedDB 存储配额与平台有关，视频格式并非全部保证可播放。
- `npm run check` 通过不等于 Desktop 实机视觉验证成功。
- 已采用 MIT 开源许可证，仍需完成真机验收与正式发布确认。

## 许可证

代码以 [MIT License](LICENSE) 授权，版权声明 `Copyright (c) 2026 deepseaandhighsky-arch`。本项目是非官方的第三方插件，与 DeepSeek 无隶属或认可关系。详见 [第三方声明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

plugins.description: Manage archived DeepSeek Harness sessions: list, restore, and permanently delete with immediate sidebar synchronization.
plugins.readme_text:
# Archived Sessions for DeepSeek Harness

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Manage archived conversations in DeepSeek Harness: view, restore or permanently delete them. Deleted conversations disappear from the sidebar immediately.

## Features

- View archived sessions, including title, workspace, creation time and log size.
- Restore archived conversations to the workspace.
- Permanently delete conversation logs without creating a backup.
- Remember the deletion confirmation preference after you acknowledge it and confirm.
- English and Simplified Chinese UI.

## Installation

Version **v0.1.1**, developed for DSH **0.2.0-rc.2**.

| System | Paste this link into Desktop's Add plugin dialog |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `https://github.com/Jeffry-Z/dsh-plugin-archived-sessions#v0.1.1` |
| macOS | `https://github.com/Jeffry-Z/dsh-plugin-archived-sessions#v0.1.1` |

Both systems use the same version and installation link.

1. Open **DeepSeek Harness Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin**.
2. Paste the link above, click **Install**, then **Enable now**.
3. Fully quit and reopen DSH, then open **Settings → Archived sessions**.

No terminal commands or manual download are needed. Validation scope: [release notes](CHANGELOG.md).

## Update and uninstall

- **Update:** uninstall the old plugin in Desktop, then install the link for the new version, enable it and fully restart DSH.
- **Uninstall:** open **Plugins**, select `dsh-plugin-archived-sessions`, click **Uninstall** and confirm.

## Usage

**Restore** keeps conversation files. **Delete** permanently removes them and cannot be undone. Checking the confirmation's “Don't ask again” option and confirming saves your choice in browser storage.

Click **Refresh** to load archive changes made elsewhere. A legacy backup section appears only when earlier versions left backups.

## Implementation

A Cordis bundle mounts the host service and a browser module adds the settings page. Deletion releases the tracked session handle, removes its files and workspace membership, emits DSH's existing removal event, then clears the archived state. Node's native path rules handle Windows and macOS directories.

The plugin does not modify DSH's installed packages. Source: [host service](lib/index.js), [lifecycle](lib/lifecycle.js), [path validation](lib/paths.js), [Remote adapter](lib/protocol.js), [settings page](lib/client.js).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) · [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)

plugins.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin to install and manage local inference providers like Strata, Ninfer, VLLM, llama.cpp, and more. 一款 DeepSeek Harness 插件，用于安装和管理 Strata、Ninfer、vLLM、llama.cpp 等本地推理服务提供商。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-local-infer

[中文 (Chinese)](docs/zh/README.md)

> For those who want more performance out of their specific hardware than what Unsloth gives out of the box.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--alpha.3-blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)
[![Type: DSH Plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Type-DSH%20Plugin-8A2BE2)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines:

- llama.cpp
- NInfer
- Hyper-Qwen (vLLM)
- Strata
- ...with more coming soon.

![Plugin Screenshot](docs/screenshot-20261014.png)

Pick a model and an engine, tune the parameters, watch a live **VRAM Est.** meter, see **hardware warnings** the moment a value (or a parameter itself) is unsafe for the detected hardware, then the plugin manages **build, deploy, and health-check** for each engine and **automatically register it as a DSH model** once it is confirmed working. No hand-editing of finicky yaml or launchers.

## Install

Command line:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer
```

Web UI: click **Plugins** → **Add Plugin** → paste `https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer`.

## Using the plugin

The **Engine settings** card mounts on the Plugins page (older hosts: the Settings page).

- **Pick an engine and model**, then tune the parameters. Each field renders by its type: checkboxes, dropdowns, sliders, text, directory pickers, and a chat-template combo (known templates plus free text).
- **Watch the VRAM Est. meter.** It prices weights, KV cache, overhead, and workspace against your card as you adjust values, and shows the verdict (`fits` / `tight` / `over`) and the largest context that fits.
- **Read the warnings.** Red banners and inline field warnings fire when a parameter value, or the presence of a parameter, is unsafe for your detected hardware.
- **Satisfy the system dependencies.** The panel lists each missing host dependency (docker, CUDA toolkit, ffmpeg, hf CLI, ...) with its purpose, a copy/paste install string for your OS, and an optional one-click **Run** (sudo). The **Get** button stays disabled until every dependency reports satisfied.
- **Launch / Stop.** `Launch` clones or pulls the engine, downloads the model, starts it, and polls its health endpoint. `Stop` shuts it down.
- **Register / Remove.** `Register` publishes the confirmed-working engine to DSH as a model (optionally as the agent default model) through the settings service, so the change is revision-tracked and undoable. `Remove` pulls the entry back.

All values persist to `~/.dsh/local-infer/config.json`; the browser never sees a value it did not store.

## Supported Platforms

### Operating systems

| OS                           | State     | Notes                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, `apt`) | Supported | Install blocks mirror the working NInfer launcher: the CUDA keyring sequence plus the compile toolchain.            |
| Linux (Arch, `pacman`)       | Supported | `pacman` blocks plus the `/opt/cuda` export lines.                                                                  |
| Linux (Fedora, `dnf`)        | Untested  | Command set present, flagged untested on a live host.                                                               |
| macOS (`brew`)               | Partial   | CPU/docker path (llama.cpp). No NVIDIA Container Toolkit on macOS, so the CUDA engines' docker path is unavailable. |
| Windows (WSL2)               | Untested  | WSL2 is detected and the dflash2 pin-memory rule fires; the command set is flagged untested.                        |
| Windows                      | Partial   | Code paths are only partially written; further development needed.                                                  |  

### Engines

| Engine            | Docker        | Local build        | State                                                                        |
|-------------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NInfer            | Yes           | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | The reference engine. Measured VRAM models for the Qwen 27B/35B artifacts.   |
| Hyper-Qwen (vLLM) | Yes (compose) | No                 | `.env`-driven docker-compose profiles.                                       |
| vLLM              | No            | No                 | Work-in-progress.                                                            |
| llama.cpp         | Yes           | Yes                | Specified, not verified until the binary is available.                       |
| Strata            | Yes           | No                 | Placeholder engine; its parameter surface is empty until the flag set lands. |

Runtime requirements: Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, pnpm 12.11.2 (pinned by `mise.toml`), and the `@deepseek-ai/cordis >= 4.0.1` peer dependency.

## Hardware guide

What each common machine gets you in practice. Capability impressions are sourced from [r/LocalLLaMA](https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/) user threads. "Shared" means unified memory (the model and the OS share the pool).

| Hardware                        | Memory          | What you get                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090                 | 32 GB VRAM      | Reliably fits model weights up to 23 GB with 240k+ context and vision. Handles complex coding and vision tasks, but needs special tooling for very long or complex tasks.     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The community workhorse. 30B-class models fit at Q4 and drive coding agents; 70B needs slow CPU offload. Best speed-per-dollar single card.                                   |
| NVIDIA RTX 3090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The used-card value king. Same 24 GB as a 4090 but an older generation: 32B at Q4 with modest context, no FP8. A single card is limiting; the common advice is to pair two.   |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000             | 96 GB VRAM      | Near-frontier dense models (70B–80B) fit fully in memory with long context, and 32B models can even be fine-tuned (LoRA, full FT). The prosumer ceiling.                      |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500             | 84 GB VRAM      | The rack-oriented 84 GB tier: 70B-class models with headroom, close to the PRO 6000 at a lower price point.                                                                   |
| NVIDIA Tesla V100               | 32 GB VRAM      | Cheap used HBM2 server card. 30B-class at Q4/Q8 at respectable speed (bandwidth is what matters for inference); no FP8, power-hungry. A budget homelab pick.                  |
| NVIDIA Tesla V100               | 16 GB VRAM      | The budget entry. 13B–14B at Q8, or 30B with offload. NVLink pairs double the capacity. Slow by modern standards, surprisingly solid for inference.                           |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 Laptop          | 24 GB VRAM      | The mobile 4090. 32B at Q4 just fits; realistically ~17B at Q4 once you subtract context.                                                                                     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 Laptop          | 16 GB VRAM      | The GPU is overkill for LLMs and the VRAM is underkill: 8B–14B at Q4/Q5 with small context.                                                                                   |
| NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)         | 128 GB shared   | The desktop AI dev box. A 35B

plugins.description: Browse your Tripsy trips inside a DeepSeek Harness panel: itinerary, activities, lodging, transport and expenses, with times in each item's own timezone. Read-only by design -- create and edit by asking the agent.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tripsy

Browse your **[Tripsy](https://tripsy.app)** trips inside a DeepSeek Harness panel: itinerary, activities, lodging, transport and expenses — with the times converted into each item's own timezone.

[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) | English

---

## What it does

A sidebar entry and a center-column page.

**＋ New trip** sits at the top of the trip list. Describe what you want in plain language — where, how long, who with, what you like — and the panel composes a detailed instruction that the agent turns into a real itinerary: the trip itself first, then activities, lodging and transport filled in day by day.

**Pick a trip** and it opens with two modules inside it:

- **行程浏览 / Browse** — a cover hero with the trip name, countdown, duration and date range; a day-grouped timeline with an icon per stop; and a cost card totalling each category from the items' own prices. Every time is rendered in its own IANA timezone.
- **AI 管理 / Manage** — describe the change you want, then press one button. The panel composes a precise instruction for that trip (id, dates and timezone included) and **sends it straight to the conversation**, so the agent starts working immediately and you watch every step. There is no prompt text to read and nothing to paste. If no conversation is open yet, the panel says so up front and the button falls back to copying the instruction.

**Your account details never reach the browser.** `/api/dsh-tripsy/health` returns only the auth summary and the account currency — not the name, e-mail or avatar the Tripsy profile carries.

```
┌ Tripsy ─────────────────────────────────┐
│ ┌ ＋ 新建行程 ─────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ 用一句话让 AI 生成行程                │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│ ┌──────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │
│ │ New York City    │ 行程浏览 │ AI 管理 │ │
│ │ 10-11 → 10-17    ├───────────────────┤ │
│ │ 东京周末         │  ╔═════════════╗  │ │
│ │                  │  ║    封面     ║  │ │
│ │                  │  ╚═════════════╝  │ │
│ │                  │  10月11日 星期日   │ │
│ │                  │  ● ✈️ LAX → JFK   │ │
│ │                  │  │ 🚗 驾车到酒店  │ │
│ │                  │  ● 🏨 Aman        │ │
│ └──────────────────┴───────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ta-www/dsh-tripsy
```

Refresh the page. **Tripsy** appears in the sidebar. The first time, click **登录 Tripsy / Sign in** — the browser opens once for the OAuth handshake, and the token then refreshes itself indefinitely.

## Trip costs, completed by the agent

Tripsy's own expense reporting needs a paid plan, so the panel works from the prices already attached to activities, lodgings and transports. The **费用概览** card in each trip sums what has a price, and **AI 计算费用** hands the agent an instruction that completes it.

The split is deliberate. Summing prices is arithmetic, so it happens on the host, exactly, once, and is tested. Estimating what has *no* price is judgement, so it goes to the agent — with the real numbers attached, and told to adopt them rather than re-estimate, to say when it is unsure instead of inventing precision, and never to assume an exchange rate. Multi-currency sums are reported per currency and never silently added together.

The card is always rendered. Keying it on a non-empty price list hid it on exactly the trips that need it most — a real imported trip has 16 items and no prices at all.

The instruction asks the agent to research each unpriced item on named platforms (大众点评 / 美团 / 抖音团购 / 小红书 domestically; Google Maps, Tripadvisor, Yelp or official pages elsewhere; 12306, 航旅纵横 or airline sites for transport), to state the source and when it was checked, and to say "couldn't find it" with a range rather than invent a precise number with a fake citation. It reports a table first and writes the prices back only once that table is confirmed, so the card then shows real totals.

The prompt also states that nothing else about the trip may be added or deleted: filling in prices is the only permitted write.

## Export to your calendar (.ics)

Each trip has **导出到日历 / Export to calendar** next to its name, and a **教程 / Guide** button that opens the import steps right there — the two halves of "get this onto my phone" are useless apart.

`GET /api/dsh-tripsy/ics?id=<tripId>` returns a `text/calendar` file:

- the trip itself as one all-day event, with the end date written exclusively (+1 day) so the last day is not lost
- every activity, lodging and transport as its own event, with `LOCATION`, `GEO`, confirmation codes, prices and notes
- items without a start time are skipped, and the count is reported in `X-Tripsy-Skipped`

**Times are absolute UTC instants, not TZID-anchored wall times.** Anchoring to a named zone is only correct when the file also carries a `VTIMEZONE` with that zone's real transitions; hand-writing those gets DST wrong and shifts events by an hour. UTC cannot be misread by any calendar and keeps flight durations truthful. The local wall time is written into each description instead, so the itinerary still reads the way the booking does.

On iPhone: save the `.ics`, then hand it to a Shortcut (the community *ICS To Calendar* one, or three actions of your own: receive Files → Choose from Calendar → Add New Event) or just tap the file and let iOS ask which calendar to use.

## How it works

The host half registers a small route family and carries its own OAuth 2.1 + MCP client in `lib/tripsy/`, so installing the plugin needs no separate service and there is exactly one implementation of the OAuth dance and one place a token is refreshed.

| | |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | host half: `/api/dsh-tripsy/{health,trips,trip,login}` |
| `lib/client.js` | browser half: the sidebar row and the panel page |
| `lib/tripsy/*.mjs` | OAuth 2.1 (PKCE + dynamic client registration), Streamable HTTP MCP client |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | inserts the plugin row |

Credential at rest: `$DSH_HOME/tripsy-auth.json` (override with the `authFile` config). It is never sent to the browser — the panel only ever sees the data, never the token.

Requests are refused unless they come from loopback. Set `allowRemote: true` in the plugin config if you deliberately serve the UI over a LAN address.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: ui-tripsy
  name: dsh-tripsy
  config:
    authFile: 'C:\Users\you\.dsh\tripsy-auth.json'   # where the token lives
    allowRemote: false                               # keep loopback-only
    enabled: true
```

## Notes

- Needs an active Tripsy account. Document attachments require Tripsy Pro; everything else works on a free account.
- Times are stored as UTC by Tripsy and rendered in each item's IANA timezone, which is what the upstream API expects clients to do.
- Unofficial community plugin, not affiliated with Tripsy.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Three-level source-text pins for DeepSeek Harness that survive context compaction: recall on demand, resident background, or highlighted constraints.
plugins.readme_text:
# highlightpin

[![Check](https://github.com/sbearbug/dsh-highlightpin/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sbearbug/dsh-highlightpin/actions/workflows/check.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**Pin any selected passage; compaction cannot take it away.**

[中文](README.zh.md) · [Design](DESIGN.md) · [Evaluation](EVAL.md) · [Live evidence](docs/PROBES.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin. Select any stretch of text in a conversation — a constraint, a number, a formula, a piece of code — and pin it with one click. From then on, no matter how the context is compacted, what the model receives is that **source text**, not a summary.

## Three levels

Each pin carries its own level:

| Level | Behaviour | Good for | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **pin** (default) | Does nothing while the text is still in context; once compaction drops it, the extract text is re-inserted verbatim near the tail before the next request | Most pins | Never touches the system prompt, so it does not break the prefix cache on its own |
| **resident** | Lives in the system prompt with neutral wording: "consult it when relevant; no need to bring it up" | Important background: you want the model to match on it the moment it matters, without you mentioning it every turn | Costs one prefix-cache invalidation when you switch levels |
| **highlight** | Lives in the system prompt with emphatic wording: "follow it when relevant; if it conflicts with your latest explicit instruction, the latest instruction wins" | Constraints and priorities the model must keep honouring | Same as above; emphasis also raises how often the model brings it up on its own |

`resident` and `highlight` are deliberately two separate levels. "The model can always find it" and "the model always keeps it in mind" are different things, and emphasis has side effects of its own — so the choice is yours.

## Installation

From npm (published releases):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-highlightpin@0.1.2
```

Or straight from the GitHub source:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add 'https://codeload.github.com/sbearbug/dsh-highlightpin/tar.gz/v0.1.2'
```

On the web profile, replace `desktop` with `web`. After installing or upgrading, **fully quit and restart DSH**, then refresh the page, so that host and client both load the new version. Existing pins survive.

### Compatible DSH versions

`peerDependencies` declares `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`. The DSH plugin manager checks these peers with `semver.satisfies(runtimeVersion, range, { includePrerelease: true })` and blocks installation and activation on a mismatch.

The range carries an explicit prerelease branch on purpose: under ordinary semver semantics a single `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` does not match the `0.2.0-rc.*` builds, because node-semver admits a prerelease only when some comparator in the range shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple and itself carries a prerelease tag.

| DSH version | Status |
|---|---|
| 0.2.0-rc.2 | **Verified live** — development and real-machine checks both ran on this version |
| 0.1.7-rc.1 / 0.1.7-rc.2 | **Offline suite passes**; CI re-runs the same suite against this line on every push |
| Other 0.2.x | Inferred from the APIs used, not verified individually |
| ≤ 0.1.6 | **Unsupported**: `CommandDefinitionId` does not exist at 0.1.5 and below, and the 0.1.6 line's session-event validation already differs |
| ≥ 0.3.0 | Not claimed |

## Usage

1. Select text inside **one** finished user or assistant message.
2. Click the pin above the composer.
3. Click the arrow beside it to open the details panel: switch each pin between "recall / resident / highlight", check budget usage, or unpin.

When you select inside a formula, the selection is expanded to the whole formula and what gets stored is the TeX source. Select the rendered $\nabla_\theta J(\theta)$ and the plugin stores `$\nabla_\theta J(\theta)$` — not the glyphs on screen. Selections inside code keep their indentation and line breaks.

Everything is also available from the command line:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/hlpin list` | List every pin, its level and budget usage |
| `/hlpin last` | Pin the most recent assistant reply in full |
| `/hlpin show <n>` | Show one pin's full text |
| `/hlpin drop <n>` | Unpin |
| `/hlpin level <n> pin\|resident\|highlight` | Change a pin's level |

## Design notes

- **What is stored is source text, not screen text.** The client serialises the selection first (formulas back to TeX, copy buttons and line numbers stripped out), and the host then locates the matching source substring in the session log. Alignment reports one of three fidelities: `source-exact` (a clean hit), `source-normalized` (matched after whitespace and Markdown normalisation, but still storing a source slice), or `rendered` (no match — it stores the display text and **tells you so**).
- **`pin` only re-inserts after the original is gone.** Right after pinning, the text is already in context, so re-injecting it would be pointless. It comes back only once compaction has shadowed it — and at that moment the prefix cache was already invalidated. So the default level cannot break caching by construction.
- **The decision is a pure function that keeps no ledger.** Every step re-decides from "is this text still in context", and records nothing like "already re-inserted". A rejected step, a plugin restart, or the recall notice itself being compacted later therefore cannot lose a pin.
- **The resident section and the recall notice never duplicate each other.** Each step records which pins actually went into the system prompt for that step, and the recall path excludes them. With no such record it re-inserts as usual: better to duplicate than to lose.
- **Over budget means rejection, not truncation.** `pin`, `resident` and `highlight` each have their own character pool. Adding or promoting past a pool's budget is rejected outright with an error code; demotion is always allowed. The plugin never quietly truncates, evicts, or demotes a pin.
- **The session log format is left alone.** Pins live in the official `storageDomain`, and recall uses a message type the host already has, so a session can never become unloadable from an unknown event. The HTTP API is origin-checked and accepts JSON only from the local page.

The full set of trade-offs is in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Verification status

- **Live**: "pin → `/compact` → next message" has been run end-to-end in DSH. The shadowed source text appeared in the next request's input, byte-identical to what was stored, with a matching SHA-256. Evidence: [docs/PROBES.md](docs/PROBES.md) and [docs/m1-live-0.1.4.json](docs/m1-live-0.1.4.json).
- **Offline**: alignment, selection serialisation, the decision function, all three injection paths, budgets, routes, commands and React interaction are covered by tests, run by CI on every push.


## Configuration

```json
{ "maxPinChars": 16000, "maxResidentChars": 6000, "maxHighlightChars": 2000, "holdSubagents": false }
```

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxPinChars` | 16000 | Total source characters across `pin` pins |
| `maxResidentChars` | 6000 | Total source characters across `resident` pins |
| `maxHighlightChars` | 2000 | Total source characters across `highlight` pins |
| `holdSubagents` | `false` | Whether subagent sessions are covered too (off by default, to avoid wasting tokens) |

Characters are counted in UTF-16 units. Neither the number of pins nor the length of a single pin is capped; only the total per level is.

## Limitations

- Selections must stay within a single message; cross-message selections are not supported.
- Streaming messages, reasoning content and tool output are not supported.
- Pins belong to one session; forked sessions do not inherit them.
- One writer host per profile is supported.
- "Highlight" here is an emphasis level in the model input; it does not draw a visual highlight on the original message.


## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run check   # build the client + run all te

plugins.description: Onto space panel for DeepSeek Harness: declarations, agents, memory and per-chat context.
plugins.readme_text:
# Onto Space Panel for DeepSeek Harness

A compact Onto space picker and a side panel for declarations, resident agents,
memory artifacts, templates and objects. Select what belongs in the current chat;
the active context remains visible above the composer.

## Features

- Connect to Onto on first use: enter your MCP endpoint and API key, verify
  access, then select a space. Reuse an existing Harness connection automatically.
- Search and select available Onto spaces.
- Open the space panel with **Обзор**.
- Read an accepted/current space declaration and attach it to the chat.
- Inspect resident agents and their charters. Selecting a valid active resident
  loads its accepted charter and constitution into the current chat.
- Search and page through accepted memory artifacts, read their contents and
  explicitly attach or disconnect them.
- Browse templates and objects, then include selected objects in the conversation.
- Keep selections and context separate for each chat and each selected realm.
- Change context through the `select_onto_space` and
  `configure_onto_chat_context` model tools when the user requests it.

The UI is currently in Russian. Names and descriptions are supplied by Onto.
An agent selection gives the current Harness conversation a resident role;
it does not launch a separate agent process or external agent broker.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with its Web UI or Desktop application.
- Your Onto MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, or an existing authenticated
  Harness MCP connection named **`onto`**.
- Harness's writable credential provider for the first-use setup form. Standard
  local profiles use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local`.
- The connection must expose `list_available_realms`, `about_realm`,
  `list_realm_agents`, `get_realm_agent`, `search_memory_artifacts`,
  `get_memory_artifact`, `get_memory_artifact_by_path`, `search_templates`,
  `search_objects` and `get_entity` for their respective panel features.

Host integration was developed against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2**.
Other releases are not yet verified. Harness is in developer preview and its
extension interfaces can change.

## Install a release tarball

Download the package `.tgz` from the project's release and install it into a
Web-capable profile. For example:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-onto-space-panel-1.2.1.tgz
```

Release downloads: https://github.com/hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel/releases

You can also install the tagged GitHub source, which already contains the built
browser entry point and has no install-time build script:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:hope4b/dsh-onto-space-panel#v1.2.1
```

In Desktop, use **Plugins** to install the downloaded bundle where supported by
your version. The tarball already contains the browser bundle; no install-time
build script or extra build permission is needed.

If this plugin was previously loaded manually by an absolute-path row in
`cordis.patch.yml`, disable that old row before enabling the packaged bundle.
Do not run two copies: they register the same tools and API routes.

Restart Harness after installing or replacing the bundle. Select an Onto space
above the composer and press **Обзор** to open its panel. Use **В контекст** to
attach a declaration or memory artifact. A role or material can be removed using
the `×` next to its context label.

## Connect Onto MCP

### First-use setup (recommended)

1. Install the plugin and restart Harness.
2. Click **Onto → Подключить** above the composer.
3. Enter your MCP endpoint URL and personal API key, then press **Подключить**.
   The key field expects only the value. A pasted `X-Onto-Api-Key: value` line
   is accepted too: the plugin removes the header name before sending or storing it.
4. The plugin checks access with `list_available_realms` before saving. After
   success, select a space from the list. An empty list means the connection
   works but no accessible spaces were returned.

Obtain the endpoint and key from your Onto administrator. The form uses HTTPS
and the `X-Onto-Api-Key` header; localhost HTTP is supported for development.
It requires a direct MCP endpoint, without credentials or query parameters in
the URL. Authentication redirects are rejected.

The connection belongs to the active Harness profile. Keys are stored through
Harness's credential provider, not in plugin configuration, browser storage or
chat messages. With the standard local provider, the managed credential file is
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`. This is local credential storage, not a claim of
OS keychain encryption. The server address and credential reference are stored
under `$DSH_HOME/storages/onto-connections/`, keyed by the profile location.
The plugin restores its own MCP connection on startup without editing profile YAML.

Open **Подключение** in the space picker, or **Подключение Onto** in the side
panel, to update a connection created by the plugin. A blank key reuses the saved
key only when the endpoint stays the same. Changing the endpoint or account key
requires choosing spaces and attaching context again; old chat context is not
automatically applied to the new connection.

If Harness already provides a server named `onto`, the plugin reuses it and
skips onboarding. Those external settings remain managed in Harness; the panel
does not overwrite or migrate that connection. A configured but unavailable
connection is shown as configured, with errors when loading spaces.

### Manual Harness configuration (fallback)

Use this when your deployment manages MCP centrally or does not provide a writable
credential provider. If the profile already has an Onto connection, do not add
a second one.

1. Obtain your Onto **MCP endpoint URL** and personal API key from your Onto
   administrator. Use the MCP endpoint, not the ordinary Onto website URL.
2. Open the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: normally
   `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` for Web or
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml` for Windows Desktop.
   A custom `DSH_HOME` changes the `.dsh` location.
3. Append the following patch, replacing the placeholder URL. If an Onto entry
   already exists, update it instead of creating a duplicate. The server name
   must be exactly `onto`.

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-onto
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: onto
        transport: streamable-http
        url: https://YOUR-ONTO-MCP-HOST/mcp
        headers:
          X-Onto-Api-Key: !!js process.env.ONTO_API_KEY
```

This example uses Onto's `X-Onto-Api-Key` header. Confirm the authentication
scheme with your server administrator if your deployment differs.
A copy is available in [examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml](examples/onto-mcp.patch.yml).

4. Set `ONTO_API_KEY` in the environment of the process that starts Harness.
   For Web on Windows, start it from the same PowerShell window:

```powershell
$env:ONTO_API_KEY = 'YOUR_PERSONAL_API_KEY'
dsh --profile web
```

For Windows Desktop, fully quit Harness first, set the variable above, then
launch the executable from that same PowerShell window. For the default installer
location:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe"
```

Launching via an existing desktop shortcut does not inherit a variable set only
in this PowerShell window. The variable must be available on every launch.
Enter your real key locally; do not commit it or share terminal history containing it.

5. Open the space selector above the composer. Your accessible spaces should
   appear. You can also ask the model to call `mcp__onto__list_available_realms`.

If connection fails, check the endpoint and network access first. A `401` or
`403` response usually indicates authentication or access rights. If the tools
work in chat but the panel cannot find them, check that `serverName` is `onto`.
Missing agent or memory tools affect those sections separately; an empty list
can also mean your account has no access to those resources.

The transport and environment-variable syntax follow the official
[Harness MCP client configuration](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepse

plugins.description: DSH 长任务（下载/编译/安装）跑完了，agent 却因为那一轮已经结束而不再说话？让它自己回来报告。DeepSeek Harness plugin that wakes the agent when a long background task finishes after its turn has ended.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-proactive · the night watchman

> A DSH plugin that lets the agent **speak up on its own** when a long job finishes
> after its turn has already ended — no more coming back to ask "is it done yet?".

[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-63%20passing-brightgreen)](#test-suite)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

[中文说明 →](README.zh-CN.md)

---

## What it does

You ask the agent to do something that takes hours — pull down a 40 GB model, wait for a
compile, sit through an installer. The agent starts the job, the turn ends, and it goes to
sleep. The job is still running. **Nothing tells the agent when it finishes**, so nothing
tells you either: you have to wander back and ask.

This plugin makes DSH watch the condition for you. When it is met, the plugin injects one
message into the session and wakes the agent — so the agent reports to you by itself.

```
you:      fetch that 20 GB thing and tell me when it's done
agent:    (starts the download → turn ends → asleep)
            ...hours later...
plugin:   *sees the file size stop changing* → *injects a message* → *wakes the agent*
agent:    "Done — 20.3 GB, and I verified the checksum against the published one."
```

## Why it exists

An agent is a request/response process. Once a turn is over it has no clock, no timer and no
way to learn that a `curl` it launched has exited or that a file has appeared on disk. Under
DSH the only thing that can hand it that fact is a message arriving in its inbox — which is
exactly what a session looks like when *you* type something. If nothing sends one, the agent
stays asleep until a human pokes it.

So the missing piece is not the waiting, it is the *waking*. This plugin is the thing that
wakes it.

## Mechanics

The wake-up uses the same call DSH itself uses when a subagent reports back to its parent
agent (see `dsh-subagent/lib/continuation.js`):

```js
agent.steer(createUserMessage({
    content: [{ type: 'text', text: message }],
    source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'dsh-proactive' },
}))
```

`agent.steer(...)` is the door into a session that is not currently running a turn;
`createUserMessage(...)` builds the message object that door expects. This is DSH's own API
surface, not a private back channel.

`source.kind = 'plugin'` is the default, and it matters: a plugin-originated message **is not
rendered in the UI**. You do not see a fake bubble pretending to be something you typed —
you only see the agent's reply, which is the whole point. `source.kind = 'user'` is available
per-entry if you deliberately want the message rendered as a user bubble, and it is used by
the test suite to prove the difference is real.

## Trigger types

| `type` | Fires when | Required fields |
|---|---|---|
| `file-stable` | The file size is unchanged across `rounds` consecutive checks — **the standard "download finished" test** | `path`, `rounds` (default `stableRounds`, 3) |
| `file-exists` | The path exists **as a file** (a directory does not count) | `path` |
| `file-size` | The file exists and its size is ≥ `bytes` | `path`, `bytes` (default 0) |
| `process-exit` | The named process is gone — **the job it was doing is over** | `process` (e.g. `curl.exe`) |
| `port-open` | A TCP connection to `host:port` succeeds — **the service came up** | `port`, `host` (default `127.0.0.1`) |
| `time` | The clock passes `at` — an alarm | `at` (ISO date-time; bare = local, `Z` = UTC) |

Unknown types never fire; they are skipped silently rather than guessed at.

### Common fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Identifies the entry in `boot.log` and in the default message. Any string. |
| `message` | What the agent reads when it wakes. Write it as an instruction to the agent, not as a note to yourself. |
| `sessionId` | Optional. Wake only this session. If it is not open, the entry is skipped for that tick and stays armed — it is **never** redirected to another session. Omit to wake the most recently active one. |
| `sourceKind` | Optional. `plugin` (default, not rendered) or `user` (rendered as a user bubble). |
| `form` | Optional, with `sourceKind: 'plugin'`. Free-form tag on the source; `notice` also carries a `summary` (first 120 chars of `message`). |
| `repeatSeconds` | Optional. Re-arm instead of firing once — see below. |

### Which session gets woken

When several DSH sessions are open, exactly one is chosen:

1. **`sessionId` set** → only that session. If it does not exist the entry is skipped, logged,
   and left armed. Refusing to fire is deliberate: a reminder delivered to the wrong session
   is worse than no reminder.
2. **`sessionId` absent** → the **most recently active** session. Activity means a message
   arrived in its inbox, its status turned `running`, or the session started. Not "the last
   one registered" — that older rule woke the wrong session when two were open, and it is
   pinned by five tests (`C. session selection`).

### One-shot versus repeating

A fired entry is stamped `fired: true` and never fires again. With `repeatSeconds` the entry
is **re-armed** instead, and `firedCount` / `lastFiredAt` record the history:

- `time` → `at` moves to now + `repeatSeconds`.
- `file-size` → `bytes` is raised to the current file size + 1, so the next byte appended
  fires it again.
- Any other type → `repeatSeconds` is meaningless and the entry silently degrades to one-shot.

Entries whose files are actually a moving target (a growing log, a progress file) are what
`repeatSeconds` is for.

## Install

One command, straight from the repository:

```bash
dsh plugin add --profile web github:mili1360/dsh-proactive
```

That resolves the package over git, adds it to the profile's `dependencies`, and registers
the bundle in `dsh.profile.bundles` on its own — verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`. Then **restart
DSH**: a registered bundle is only picked up at boot.

Works the same way from a local clone, if you would rather build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mili1360/dsh-proactive.git
dsh plugin add --profile web ./dsh-proactive
```

<details>
<summary>Doing it by hand instead</summary>

The plugin imports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, so it has to sit somewhere Node can resolve that
package from — a normal place for that is inside the profile's module tree.

```bash
# 1. put the plugin next to (or inside) your DSH profile
git clone https://github.com/mili1360/dsh-proactive.git ./dsh-proactive

# 2. register it in <profile>/package.json
#    dependencies:        "dsh-proactive": "link:<absolute path to the plugin>"
#    dsh.profile.bundles: [ "dsh-proactive" ]      <- add to the array
```

Then verify the import resolves from the plugin directory:

```bash
node -e "import('@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm').then(m => console.log('createUserMessage =', typeof m.createUserMessage))"
# createUserMessage = function
```

If that fails, link the package the way DSH exposes it — for example a `node_modules/@deepseek-ai`
junction inside the plugin directory pointing at `<profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai`.

**Restart DSH.** `dsh.marketplace.requiresRestart` is `true`, and a newly registered bundle is
not picked up without one. Afterwards the plugin directory contains `boot.log`, and three
lines mean it loaded:

```
apply() 被调用  enabled=true  intervalMs=15000
定时器已挂载
守夜人就绪
```

No `boot.log` means the bundle never loaded — check the profile registration again.

</details>

## Requirements / compatibility

**After installing, confirm it actually works — a profile that boots is not proof.**
A plugin can load cleanly, serve its routes and still break the host; we have seen exactly
that. So the acceptance test is: **create a new session and send it one message** (the plugin
is idle until a watch fires, so a quiet log is expected), then confirm the session exists and
the agent answered. If new sessions cannot be created at all, remove the mount line above and
restart.

Developed and tested against DSH **`0.1.0-rc.7`** — a **customised** build, not a stock
upstream release. Another version may register its services or name its events differently:
this plugin uses `ctx.on`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.agents`, the `agent/created`,
`agent/sessi

plugins.description: Community plugin for DeepSeek Harness: a lighter LLM service with self-contained provider profiles, a declared model catalog, and the chat-completions, Anthropic Messages, and OpenAI Responses wires. Not an official DeepSeek package.
plugins.readme_text: # @snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite English | [中文](README.zh.md) > **Community plugin.** Maintained by [snnh](https://github.com/snnh). It is not > an official DeepSeek package: DeepSeek neither publishes nor supports it, and > issues belong in this repository. ## Install A harness loads plugins from a profile's own installation, so this package is installed into a profile rather than into the harness itself: ```sh # From the published package: dsh plugin --profile web add @snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite # Or straight from this repository. pnpm builds the checkout while installing, # which the profile must allow first: run the command, add the exact key pnpm # printed under `allowBuilds` in /pnpm-workspace.yaml, and re-run it. dsh plugin --profile web add github:snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite ``` ### Mount The package declares itself a bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch`), so the install above also mounts its `llm-service-lite` row: one command installs and mounts, and no hand-written entry is needed. The mount is dormant — no route exists until a profile declares one. Two surfaces edit the same document. In the web UI, open **Plugins**, select this bundle, open its `llm-service-lite` row, and choose **Configure**: the page lists every provider, adds and removes profiles, edits the endpoint, protocol, capabilities and model catalog, stores an API key through the harness credential service, and asks an endpoint which models it serves. The same document can be edited by hand in the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` (`$DSH_HOME/profiles//cordis.patch.yml`; **Settings → Open configuration file** in the web UI opens it). Add the `providers` dictionary described under [Configure provider profiles](#configure-provider-profiles) to the `llm-service-lite` row's `config`. The profile patch is applied after every bundle layer, so that entry's `config` replaces the row's empty default; the same entry also mounts the plugin in a composition that declares no bundle layer, because it names the module to load: ```yaml - id: llm-service-lite name: '@snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite' config: providers: # ... provider profiles, one per endpoint ``` After the install, refresh the Web page once: the browser half is served by the client module system, so the new page appears on the **Plugins** screen the next time the shell boots. It lives on the bundle's page and on its `llm-service-lite` row, where that row's **Configure** control opens it. The plugin fills the **Models** page's adapter-family extension seats while the Host serves its settings namespace: every `llm-service-lite` provider card gets the plugin's own editor, and the section footer gets the same add-provider builder. The builder asks for a preset, route, protocol, endpoint, optional key, and runs a connection test before writing; the editor covers protocol, endpoint, credential, request behavior, a connection test, and the model catalog. The catalog is a filterable list with one expanded model editor; effort levels and thinking modes are localized toggles, and **Fill capabilities** applies the documented family defaults to fields a model left open. `extraBody` sits behind an advanced disclosure and blocks a save when its JSON is malformed. The plugin's page on the **Plugins** screen edits the same row `config`. Hand-written fields it does not render (`headers`, `imageTokens`, `imagePixelBudget`, `imageMaxBytes`, `catalog`, `retryPolicy`, and the per-model `defaults`) are preserved by every save and remain editable in the patch. Credentials are named, not inlined, in a managed profile: set `apiKeyEnv` to the reference (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, say) and store the secret through the harness credential service, export it in the launching environment, or keep it in the harness home's `.env`. The reference is resolved on every request, and a named reference that resolves to nothing fails the request with `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` instead of sending it unauthenticated. A profile imported verbatim from OWCode may keep its inline `apiKey`. Mount it exactly once. When a composition already carries an `llm-service-lite` row (the archived [dsh-lite](https://github.com/snnh/dsh-lite) fork's `dsh-base` bundle shipped one), that row already reaches this package: install without activating it as a bundle — `dsh plugin --profile web add -D @snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite` — and configure the existing row. Keep exactly one layer for the row: a later layer's same-id insert replaces the earlier row and its **whole `config`** — patch layers never deep-merge — so a second row silently discards what the first configured; it does not mount a second instance. ### Route names Route names must be unique across the adapters mounted in one composition. On stock upstream profiles the shipped `llm-pi-ai` catalog already declares common provider names (`deepseek`, `openai`, `anthropic`, and similar), so prefer a distinct route id that names the endpoint itself — `deepseek-direct`, `company-gateway` — rather than a name an installed catalog may own. A profile whose route name another adapter already owns is skipped with one warning naming the owner instead of failing the mount, the rest of the profiles register, and a newly written profile that claims such a name is refused where it is written; renaming its route is the repair. The plugin also refuses, by name, the routes the first-party DeepSeek channel owns; see [Use this package](#use-this-package). ### Compatibility This package drives the public seam of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` and the `@deepseek-ai/cordis` service layer, so it runs against a published harness rather than a checkout: its peers are the harness packages, and the profile that loads it already owns the copies the runtime uses. The development baseline is harness `0.2.1-rc.2` — `devDependencies` pin those packages and the test suite runs against them — while the `^0.2.1-alpha.2` peer ranges also admit the `0.2.1` alpha line, so an older `0.2.1` harness loads the same package. Two declarations of the archived [dsh-lite](https://github.com/snnh/dsh-lite) fork are used when the running harness carries them and skipped when it does not: the model-defaults registration seam a configuration surface asks for declared model ids, and the `outputModalities` field on a model's info. Upstream `0.2.1-rc.2` carries neither, so both are inert there: the adapter keeps its family defaults on the request path, where they still fill the fields a profile left open, and the extra field is simply ignored by the runtime. ## Summary `@snnh/dsh-llm-service-lite` adapts third-party model endpoints: one route per configured provider profile, all answered over its transports — the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions wire, the Anthropic Messages protocol, and the OpenAI Responses API — so no provider SDK and no installed catalog sits in the request path. A profile is self-contained — wire protocol, endpoint, credential reference, request-body extras, concurrency, image input, and the models served — so a gateway, a national API, and a corporate proxy reach one code path. The shape ports OpenWebCode's model-provider layer onto the harness seam: one document describes every provider, and the route set follows it live. ## Table of Contents - [Install](#install) - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Mount this plugin when a deployment wants to describe its model providers itself instead of naming providers an installed catalog already knows. The `providers` dictionary is the whole configuration surface: each key is the provider route a request selects with `GenerateOptions.provider`, and the value is everything that endpoint needs. ### When to choose it This plugin adapts third-party endpoints and nothing else: every route it registers comes from a profile a deployment wrote, and the first-party DeepSeek channel keeps its own a

plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-license-guard

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-license-guard)


**开源许可与许可证合规**：发版前、开源前、被审计时跑一遍 —— 把 GPL/AGPL 传染、许可未知、缺 LICENSE 这几类风险找出来。

**关键词**：开源许可 · 开源协议 · 许可证合规 · 许可风险 · GPL 传染 · AGPL · 开源合规 · 许可证
**Keywords**: open source license · license compliance · GPL · AGPL · copyleft · license risk
**开源许可合规检查** —— 扫依赖树，找出 GPL/AGPL 传染、许可未知等风险。

发布前、开源前、被审计时跑一遍。退出码可挂 CI。

## 不装它会怎样

你的产物里混进了一个 **GPL 依赖**，你没发现，打包发出去了。

半年后客户审计问：「你用了 GPL 代码，为什么没开源？」——
**GPL 的义务从「分发」那一刻就触发了**，而分发在半年前。

这个检查跑一次几秒钟。

## 它查什么

| 级别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 高 | GPL / AGPL —— 强传染 |
| 🟡 中 | 许可未知（没写许可证 ≠ 随便用）· 项目缺 LICENSE |
| 🟢 低 | LGPL / MPL / EPL · package.json 缺 license 字段 |

## 安装

```bash
# DSH 插件（推荐）
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-license-guard

# 或纯 CLI（不依赖 DSH）
npx @deepwhale-cn/dsh-license-guard
```

## 用法

```bash
dsh-license-guard                # 扫当前目录
dsh-license-guard --demo         # 用内置样本看效果
dsh-license-guard --html r.html  # 输出 HTML 报告
```

![dsh-license-guard 检查报告示例](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-license-guard/report.png)

![dsh-license-guard 演示模式输出](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-license-guard/demo.png)

![dsh-license-guard 规则与依据](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-license-guard/rules.png)

## 覆盖范围

**5 条规则**，覆盖依赖树的许可风险 + 项目基础文件。

**不覆盖**：专利条款、商标、出口管制、SSPL/BUSL 等非 SPDX 自定义协议。
依赖声明的许可证值可能不准（维护者写错），本工具**不校验其真实性**。

## 为什么和其他工具不同

它**不只看依赖**，也看**你自己**：项目缺 LICENSE、package.json 缺 license 字段 ——
这两条会让别人（和你自己的下游）无法判断能不能用你的代码。

## 边界

本插件是一个工具。使用者必须遵守所在地区法律法规，**对使用本项目造成的任何后果自行承担责任。**

## 开发

```bash
npm install
bash tests/run.sh     # 双向验证（正例必须报 + 反例必须不报）
```

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 31 个）

> 一个插件做一件事。**安全问题是链式的** —— 配套用才完整。

**国内合规** ｜ [等保对照](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-mlps) · [日志留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) · [备案公示](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-filing) · [用户同意](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-consent-guard) · [个人信息权利](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-rights) · [未成年人保护](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-minor-guard) · [影响评估](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-pipia) · [数据分类分级](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-classify) · [算法备案](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-algorithm-filing) · [数据出境](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) · [国密合规](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-crypto) · [AI 内容标识](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-ai-labeling)

**AI 与 Agent 治理** ｜ [AI 输出信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ai-output-trust) · [外部内容信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-content-trust) · [MCP 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) · [Agent 权限](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-scope) · [策略核对](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-policy) · [可疑指令](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-phishing-guard)

**数据与凭据** ｜ [敏感数据](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-scan) · [密钥轮换](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-key-rotate) · [数据留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-lifecycle) · [配置审计](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-env-audit) · [密钥扫描](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-secret-scan)

**供应链与构建** ｜ [**开源许可**](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-license-guard) · [依赖投毒](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-dep-audit) · [CI 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ci-guard) · [工具审查](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-tool-vet) · [物料清单](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-sbom)

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-minimax-connect

把本机 **MiniMax Code（Mavis）** 已登录的订阅接入 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)，作为一个模型 provider，并在设置侧边栏给出一个独立页面：**积分余额 / 每日签到 / 模型清单 / 用量**。

积分制账号：不消耗 API key，消耗 MiniMax Code 订阅的积分。

> **不用打开 MiniMax Code。** 插件自己完成 OAuth 续期，桌面客户端可以完全退出。
> 详见 [凭据自续期](#凭据自续期)。

English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)

---

## 为什么不需要"反代"

MiniMax Code 的推理端点**本身就是 Anthropic Messages 协议**，DSH 的 `pi-ai` 原生支持该协议。所以直接把请求打到官方端点即可，不需要中间代理进程，也不需要 hook 客户端。

`~/.minimax/config.yaml` 里 MiniMax 自己就写着：

```yaml
provider:
  minimax:
    npm: '@ai-sdk/anthropic'
    options:
      baseURL: https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1
```

## 实测契约（全部为真实响应，非推测）

| 用途 | 方法与路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 对话 | `POST {llm}/v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages 协议；流式返回 `thinking_delta` + `text_delta` |
| 模型清单 | — | `GET {llm}/v1/models` 返回 **503 `direct_route_not_configured`**；改从本地 `config.yaml` 静态解析 |
| 续期 | `POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token` | `grant_type=refresh_token`，见下 |
| 积分 | `GET {cloud}/credit/details` | `details[]` 带 `granted_amount` / `remaining_amount` / `consumed_amount` |
| 签到面板 | `GET {cloud}/signin/status?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai` | **`timezone_id` 是必需参数**，缺则 `1406010011 invalid timezone_id` |
| 签到 | `POST {cloud}/signin/claim?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai`，body `{}` | 空 body 与官方客户端一致；**同样需要 `timezone_id`** |

其中：

```
{llm}   = https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm
{cloud} = https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1
```

**注意两个 base 不同**：Anthropic SDK 会自己在 `baseURL` 后补 `/v1/messages`，所以 `{llm}` **不带**结尾的 `/v1`；而 cloud 路由**带** `/v1`。

## 鉴权

读 `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json`，取 `records[*].accessToken`（`mmoat_` 开头），以 **`Authorization: Bearer`** 发送。

> ⚠️ **不能用 Anthropic 的 `x-api-key`**：实测报 `401 {"code":401,"message":"token is required"}`。

记录键是 `` `${service}\0${account}` ``，分隔符是**真的 NUL 字符**，`account` = `base64url(sha256(authHome + "\0" + "mcode-public"))`。

## 凭据自续期

access token **有效期 1 小时**。MiniMax Code 大致每小时续期一次并写回同一个文件 —— 在它之外没有任何东西会做这件事，所以关掉桌面客户端后，插件在 token 过期的那一刻就废了：实测过期后第一个请求回 `401 invalid access token`，而记录里躺着一个完全可用的 `refreshToken` 无人问津。

本插件自己执行同一个 grant：

```
POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token
     grant_type=refresh_token
     refresh_token=<mmort_…>
     client_id=mcode-public
     scope=agent.default
     audience=agent-backend
  -> { access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in, scope }
```

行为：

- **提前 5 分钟续期**，不让任何一条流开在一个正在死掉的 token 上。除按需触发外，还有一条 60 秒的巡检。
- **`refresh_token` 单次有效、每次 grant 都轮换**，所以旧值在应答到达的瞬间就死了，新的一对必须在用新 access token 之前落盘。写入是**原子替换**（临时文件 + rename），桌面客户端不会读到写了一半的记录。
- **与官方客户端共存**。客户端用文件锁串行化自己的续期（`proper-lockfile`，`auth.lock` → `auth.lock.lock` 目录，`stale: 30_000`）。这里复用同一套 on-disk 约定：`mkdir` 抢占、超过 30 秒的锁按陈旧回收、写入前重新读一次文件并**采纳更新的 generation 而不是覆盖它**。两边轮流续期互不踢出，已实测双向共存。
- **两个文件必须同步推进**。客户端 `MCodeOAuthCore.readUsableCredential` 要求 `credential.generation === state.generation`，不一致就当成未登录。新代际取 `max(state.generation, credential.generation) + 1` —— 只用凭据自己的计数器，就可能写回一个**低于** `auth-state.json` 的值，把账号锁在自己的新 token 外面。
- **失败不抛异常**，一律回 `{ ok: false, reason, fatal? }`，调用方继续用盘上已有的 token。`fatal` 只标记一种永久失败：`invalid_grant`（refresh token 本身没了），此时只有去 MiniMax Code 重新登录一次能把 provider 救回来。

设一面卡片会直接显示当前状态：*自动续期已启用（到期前 5 分钟），不用打开 MiniMax Code* / *正在自动续期…* / *自动续期暂停，HH:MM:SS 后重试* / *凭据没有 refreshToken，需在 MiniMax Code 里重新登录一次*。

### 端到端验证

`test/renew-e2e.mjs` 只把 `expiresAtMs` 改到"即将过期"（**两个 token 一个都不碰**，所以 grant 失败也是零代价），然后调用插件自己发货的 `renewCredential`，最后拿新 token 打真实模型端点：

```bash
node test/renew-e2e.mjs ~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json
```

在 MiniMax Code **进程数为 0** 的情况下实测通过：grant 273 ms、代际 +1、两个文件代际相等、`loginEpoch` 保留、`refreshToken` 轮换，新 token 打 `/v1/messages` 返回 **HTTP 200** `{"text":"ok","base_resp":{"status_code":0}}`。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:VICqiufeeng/dsh-minimax-connect"
```

1. 装在 profile 的 `node_modules` 下，`dsh.profile.bundles` 会自动加上这一项。
2. **重启 DSH** 后生效。
3. 本插件不写用户补丁层（不碰 `cordis.patch.yml`），卸载时从 `dependencies` 与 `dsh.profile.bundles` 两处移除即可，不留残留。

如果 pnpm 的供应链闸门报 `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`（对 git 依赖一般不触发），追加 `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0`。

## 界面

**设置 → MiniMax**（`settings.section` 插槽，order 460），四个区块：

- **积分 + 签到 + 账号** —— 通用积分余额、七天签到面板、账号信息与续期状态。
- **模型清单** —— 逐模型开关 / 图片输入 / 上下文窗口（200K 或 1M）。
- **保存行** —— 落盘到插件自己的 settings 命名空间 `llm-minimax`。

同一份卡片也会出现在**插件管理页**（侧边栏「插件」图标 → 已安装 → `dsh-minimax-connect`）的详情里，因为它同时注册了 `plugins.bundle.config` 与 `plugins.row.config`。

另有一个自包含的零构建 HTML 面板：`GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel`。

## 路由（全部仅回环）

| 路由 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/status` | 汇总快照（面板用），含 `selfRenewal` |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/usage` | 积分明细原始应答 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/checkin` | 签到状态 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin` | 七天签到面板原始应答 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin/claim` | 执行签到 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/models` | 当前模型清单 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/__save` | 写回启用模型 / 图片开关 / 上下文窗口 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel` | 自包含 HTML 面板（无构建步骤） |

## 配置

`Config`（schemastery）可覆盖的字段：

| 字段 | 默认 |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm` |
| `cloudBaseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1` |
| `authFile` | `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json` |
| `configFile` | `~/.minimax/config.yaml` |
| `cacheMs` | `15000` |
| `enabledModelIds` / `imageOverrides` / `useMaximumContextWindow` | 由设置页写入 |
| 各 `*Route` | 见上表 |

## 模型

清单来自本地 `~/.minimax/config.yaml` 的 `whitelist` + `model_order`，默认四个：

| 模型 | 上下文 | 图片 | 推理 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MiniMax-M3` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 可开关 |
| `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |

## 已知限制

- **积分不换算成本**：模型描述符的 `cost` 全为 0。积分制下没有公开的每 token 单价，填 0 好过填一个编出来的数字。
- **依赖客户端非公开接口**：MiniMax 更新后端点可能变动；端点集中在 `lib/index.js` 顶部注释里，便于对照。
- **图片输入**走宿主的 durable attachment service。老版本宿主不提供该服务时会回 `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT`，插件对两种 store 形状都做了适配。
- 只测过 **Windows + 国内版（cn）**。区域路径与 `buildEnv` 硬编码在 `defaultAuthFile()` 里，其它区域需要改这一处。

## 设计说明

代码里凡是"为什么这么写"的地方都留了注释，几处值得一读的：

- `credential renewal` 段头：为什么插件不得不接管续期。
- `mirrorAuthState` / `nextGeneration`：两个文件代际必须一致的原因，以及那个会导致锁死自己的 off-by-one。
- `withAuthLock`：为什么复刻 `proper-lockfile` 的 on-disk 约定而不是依赖它。
- `adaptAttachmentStore`：宿主 attachment store 的两种形状。
